# Renderer kit API

The public API of the renderer kit the built-in renderers use, by entry: `@githubnext/projections/kit`,
framework-free (the comparison model, step timeline, staged motion, graph layout, diff mode, status and colors), and
`@githubnext/projections/kit/react` (the shell, graph canvas, components and hooks). Read with the
`typescript-public-api` extractor; descriptions are the sources' documentation comments. Start with
[the kit's guide](../guides/renderer-kit.md).

## Framework-free (`@githubnext/projections/kit`)

### `ArrowBox`

```ts
interface ArrowBox
```

A card's box for routing arrows, in drawing units with y growing downward: its top-left corner and size.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `"height": number` | The box's height; not negative. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The box's width; not negative. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | The box's left side. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | The box's top side. |

### `arrowEnding`

```ts
arrowEnding(points: Array<Point>, target: FaceBox, outset?: number): { "base": Point; "direction": Point; "head": string; "shaft": Array<Point>; "tip": Point }
```

Where a relationship's arrowhead goes and the shaft that leads to it. The
head's painted tip stops `outset` short of the target card's face the route
reaches (how far the card's border is painted outside its box, see
`cardBorderOutset`), so it touches the border without covering it, and points
along that face's inward normal, whatever the route's own final tangent is
(ELK ends spline sections with a degenerate cubic, whose tangent is
undefined). The shaft ends at the middle of the head's flat base, after a
straight lead-in collinear with the head (`arrowHeadReach` from the tip);
the route keeps its course up to the last point before that run and curves
into it smoothly, so the shaft never enters the head at an angle.

### `arrowHead`

```ts
arrowHead(tip: Point, direction: Point): ArrowHead
```

The head at `tip`, pointing along `direction` (normalized here).

### `ArrowHead`

```ts
interface ArrowHead
```

One arrowhead's geometry, from `arrowHead`: where it touches, where its shaft ends, and its outline.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `base` | `"base": Point` | Middle of the flat base, where the shaft ends. |
| `direction` | `"direction": Point` | Unit vector from base to tip. |
| `lead` | `"lead": Point` | Where the straight lead-in begins: the shaft runs straight from here to `base`. |
| `path` | `"path": string` | The inner outline, drawn filled and stroked with `arrowHeadStrokeWidth` and round joins (see `arrowHeadStyle`): the stroke rounds its corners and grows it to the head's full size. |
| `tip` | `"tip": Point` | Where the rounded tip touches the target. |

### `arrowHeadCornerRadius`

```ts
arrowHeadCornerRadius: 1.25
```

Radius of the head's rounded corners.

### `arrowHeadLeadIn`

```ts
arrowHeadLeadIn: 6
```

The straight run of shaft before the base, collinear with the head, that a route curves into.

### `arrowHeadLength`

```ts
arrowHeadLength: 8.5
```

From the rounded tip to the flat base, along the head's axis.

### `arrowheadPath`

```ts
arrowheadPath(x: number, y: number, angle: number, size?: number): string
```

An equilateral arrowhead with rounded corners, pointing at (`x`, `y`) in
the direction `angle` (radians; 0 points right, −π/2 points up). Fill and
stroke it in one color with `stroke-linejoin: round` (the kit's
`.pk-arrowhead`); `size` is the side length.

### `arrowHeadReach`

```ts
arrowHeadReach: number
```

From the tip to where a route may stop being straight: head plus lead-in.

### `arrowHeadStrokeWidth`

```ts
arrowHeadStrokeWidth: number
```

Stroke width that rounds the inner outline's corners to `arrowHeadCornerRadius`.

### `arrowHeadStyle`

```ts
arrowHeadStyle(color: string): { "fill": string; "stroke": string; "strokeLinejoin": "round"; "strokeWidth": number }
```

Presentation attributes for an arrowhead path: filled and stroked in `color`, with round joins.

### `badgeMetrics`

```ts
badgeMetrics: { "accent": number; "gap": number; "height": number; "icon": number; "iconGap": number; "inset": number; "row": number; "tagGap": number }
```

Badge geometry: a pill's height, its text's inset, the gap between pills and the pitch of their rows; a highlight's
icon and the space after it; and the gap between quiet tags.

### `badgeText`

```ts
badgeText(badge: string | { "prose"?: true; "text": string; "tone"?: "highlight" | "quiet" }): string
```

A badge's text.

### `balancedWrap`

```ts
balancedWrap(widths: Array<number>, gap: number, available: number): BalancedWrap
```

Wraps `widths` (each item's width, in order) into as few lines as greedy
wrapping needs within `available`, then narrows the lines to the smallest
maximum width that still needs no more lines. Greedy filling at that width
keeps earlier lines at least as long as later ones; where it can't (an item
order that forces a longer last line), the break set with the smallest
widest line among the top-heavy ones is used, and if none is top-heavy,
the narrowest.

### `BalancedWrap`

```ts
interface BalancedWrap
```

Balanced wrapping for rows of items (pills, chips, tags): as few lines as
greedy wrapping needs at the available width, then lines as close to the
same width as possible, never with a later line longer than an earlier one.
Item order is kept. CSS `text-wrap: balance` works only on inline text and
doesn't promise a top-heavy result, so renderers place items with this.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `lines` | `"lines": Array<Array<number>>` | Item indices on each line, in order. |
| `widths` | `"widths": Array<number>` | Each line's width: its items plus the gaps between them. |

### `BlockedBoxEdge`

```ts
interface BlockedBoxEdge
```

No route around the cards exists (`routeBoxEdge`): `least` is the candidate that overlaps the obstacles least
(fewest cards crossed, then the shortest stretch inside them), and `crossed` the indices in `obstacles` it crosses.
Whether to draw it is the caller's policy, and drawing it should be reported.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `blocked` | `"blocked": true` | No route clears the cards. |
| `crossed` | `"crossed": Array<number>` | The indices in `obstacles` of the cards `least` crosses. |
| `least` | `"least": BoxEdge` | The candidate route that overlaps the obstacles least. |

### `BorderWidths`

```ts
interface BorderWidths
```

The theme's border widths in CSS px: `--stroke` and `--stroke-strong` (the host's border width tokens).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `normal` | `"normal": number` | A plain card's border, `--stroke`; it decides how far an arrowhead stops short of a card (`cardBorderOutset`). |
| `strong` | `"strong": number` | A change border, `--stroke-strong`, drawn inset so its outer edge matches the plain border's (`emphasisInset`). |

### `boundaryKinds`

```ts
boundaryKinds(compound: Array<string> | false | true | undefined): Array<string>
```

The entity kinds a `compound` option lets become boundaries.

### `boundaryNouns`

```ts
boundaryNouns(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction>, compound: Array<string> | false | true): { (kind: string, collection: "entities" | "relationships"): SummaryNoun | false | undefined } | { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun | false }
```

Nouns that leave grouping boundaries out of the summary: each of the boundary kinds `compound` names (see
`boundaryKinds`) whose every entity is drawn as a boundary round others (see `moduleGroups`) in each revision and,
in a comparison, in the union of both the canvas lays out for the diff and the steps between (see `unionGraph`),
maps to `false`. Such a box only groups the cards it holds, which the summary counts, so it is no figure beside them;
a kind some of whose entities are drawn as cards anywhere (a module others depend on, or one two parents hold across
the revisions) is counted whole, as the protocol counts kinds. Spread it into a renderer's nouns:
`{contains: false, ...boundaryNouns(model, true)}`.

### `boundedLegend`

```ts
boundedLegend(legend: RendererLegend): RendererLegend
```

Fits a legend to the protocol's bounds: labels are clipped, and past
`rendererLimits.legendItems` the remainder folds into one "N more" item.

### `boxEdge`

```ts
boxEdge(from: ArrowBox, target: ArrowBox, obstacles?: Array<ArrowBox>, style?: "curved" | "orthogonal", ports?: { "end"?: Point; "start"?: Point }, outset?: number, tracks?: Array<number>): BoxEdge
```

An arrow from one card to another, around `obstacles`, ending at the base
of the kit's arrowhead (draw it with `EdgeArrowMarker`). Facing sides are
joined by the kit's one clean S (see `sBend`); a downward S blocked by a
card is drafted down the nearest clear corridor between cards instead, and
failing that the arrow is routed around the cards on a grid. The head's
painted tip stops `outset` outside the target's box, on the outer edge of
its border (see `cardBorderOutset`, the default for kit cards).

### `BoxEdge`

```ts
interface BoxEdge
```

A `boxEdge` arrow: its path `d`, endpoints, and the S turns a downward route takes.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `base` | `"base": Point` | The base of the arrowhead, where the path ends. |
| `d` | `"d": string` | The SVG path, from `start` to the head's `base`. |
| `end` | `"end": Point` | The head's tip, `outset` outside the target card. |
| `start` | `"start": Point` | Where the arrow leaves its source card. |
| `turns` | `"turns"?: Array<EdgeTurn>` | The S turns a downward route takes, for `routeTracks`. |

### `boxEdgeTurn`

```ts
boxEdgeTurn(start: Point, end: Point, cards: Array<ArrowBox>, outset?: number): undefined | { "band": readonly [number, number] }
```

The S a downward `boxEdge` arrow turns on (its band and middle, see
`sTurn`), for spreading arrows that share a gap onto separate tracks
(`routeTracks`) before routing them. Undefined unless the arrow leaves a
card's bottom for another's top.

### `CardAccent`

```ts
interface CardAccent
```

A card's accent: its paint, and what it means in words (`scope: secret`), for assistive technology.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `category` | `"category"?: string` | The category the color stands for (`Rust`, a kind), when it is a categorical color: a language's own color isn't a theme token, so the band is marked `data-projections-category` with it, as categorical marks are. |
| `label` | `"label": string` | What the color means, added to the card's accessible name; empty when the card already says it (its kind). |
| `paint` | `"paint": string` | CSS paint: a color or a theme token's variable. |

### `CardBadge`

```ts
type CardBadge = string | { "prose"?: true; "text": string; "tone"?: "highlight" | "quiet" }
```

A badge: code, drawn in monospace on a pill, or `{text, prose: true}`, human words in sans on a pill. Its `tone`
sets it apart: a `highlight` (words, with a shield check, in the accent hue) is a fact to see first, such as how it
is formally verified; a `quiet` one is a code tag without a pill, muted, on rows of its own after the pills (where
it runs, say).

### `cardBorderOutset`

```ts
cardBorderOutset(widths?: BorderWidths): number
```

How far a kit card's border (an SVG stroke centred on its box) reaches outside the box: where an arrowhead's tip stops.

### `cardBox`

```ts
cardBox(node: Pick<TransitionNode, "height" | "opacity" | "width" | "x" | "y">): ArrowBox
```

A card's box at its current presence: entering and leaving cards scale from 90%.

### `cardFooterHeight`

```ts
cardFooterHeight: 18
```

The band at the bottom of every card in a comparison reserved for its change status, so status never resizes a card.

### `cardFooterRoom`

```ts
cardFooterRoom(width: number): number
```

The room for one row of text in a card's footer band (a change line such as `Lifetime Scoped → Singleton`, above
the status), in card units: the card's `width` less its text inset on each side. Footer rows are centred on the
card (see `SvgFooterRow`), so text laid out within this keeps the inset from both sides; longer text wraps onto
more rows.

### `cardHeight`

```ts
cardHeight(kind: string, footer?: false | true): number
```

A card's height: its text (one line for a file, a kind line and a label otherwise) and, unless `footer` is false
(one revision, which has no change status), the status footer under it.

### `cardIconMetrics`

```ts
cardIconMetrics: { "gap": 5; "ink": number; "size": 14 }
```

A card icon's box, in card units: `size` square, `gap` before the kind line's text, and `ink`, Lucide's margin
inside its 24-unit box at that size, which the box is pulled left by so the glyph lines up with the text below it.

The icons a graph card can show before its kind line (`GraphCanvasProps.icon`), by their Lucide names

### `cardIconRoom`

```ts
cardIconRoom: number
```

The room a card icon takes before the kind line's text: its box and the gap after it.

### `cardTextMetrics`

```ts
cardTextMetrics: { "detailGap": 8; "detailLength": 14; "fileInset": 40; "firstBaseline": 21; "footerInset": 8; "inset": 16; "labelAdvance": 7; "labelBaseline": 41; "monoAdvance": 7.4; "proseAdvance": 6.6 }
```

Graph card text in card units at the type scale's default extra-small size (12); a theme with another size scales
the advances (`textScale`, its size over 12). Advances are rounded up from monospace's 0.6 em and the sans fonts'
average, so text never needs more room than a card makes for it.

### `CardTextStyle`

```ts
type CardTextStyle = "label" | "mono" | "prose"
```

The style text is drawn in on a card: code in monospace, human text in sans, and a sans label in semibold.

### `cardTextWidth`

```ts
cardTextWidth(text: string, style: "label" | "mono" | "prose", textScale?: number): number
```

Width of `text` drawn in `style`, in card units, at `textScale` times the default size.

### `cardWidth`

```ts
cardWidth: 200
```

The width of a card laid out without one of its own; `GraphCanvas` sizes cards to their text (`graphCardWidth`).

### `cardWidthRange`

```ts
cardWidthRange: { "max": 216; "min": 112 }
```

The narrowest and widest graph card, in card units (the widest grows by an icon's room on a card with an icon, see
`GraphCanvasProps.icon`). A graph's cards share one width, what its longest card text needs between the two (see
`graphCardWidth`), so a graph of short names packs densely and its layers stay aligned;
text longer than the widest card holds is cut short with an ellipsis, and the card's tooltip has it whole.

### `Category`

```ts
interface Category
```

Colors for categories of files and languages, shared by every built-in
renderer so a language is the same color everywhere:

- Programming and markup languages take their GitHub Linguist color
  (`@githubnext/projections/renderer`), adjusted per theme
  for contrast. TypeScript is Linguist's blue in file packing and in code
  statistics alike.
- Everything else (data, configuration, prose and assets: JSON, YAML,
  TOML, Markdown, images) takes a slot of the theme's categorical palette
  (`chart-1` … `chart-16`): its preferred slot when free and clear of the
  language colors in use, otherwise the first one in palette order that is.
- Past the palette, the rest share the neutral "other" color, which nothing
  else uses.

Rank by the whole document (both revisions), so a category keeps its color
from Before to After.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `"key": string` | Identity: the language's presented name (`TypeScript` for TSX too), or `.ext`, `none` or a kind. |
| `label` | `"label": string` | Shown in the legend and tooltips. |
| `language` | `"language"?: Language` | The Linguist language, which gives the category its color; absent for categories that take a palette slot. |

### `categoryPalette`

```ts
categoryPalette(categories: Iterable<{ "category": Category; "weight": number }, any, any>, colorMode?: "dark" | "light", options?: PaletteOptions): Palette
```

Assigns colors to weighted categories (see the module notes). `colorMode`
picks the theme's language colors. Palette slots are kept clear of the
language colors in both themes' defaults, so a category takes the same slot
in each; the slots themselves are painted with the host's tokens.

### `ChangeClassification`

```ts
type ChangeClassification = "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed" | "unchanged"
```

Identity change and content change are orthogonal; presentation folds them into one label.

### `changeMark`

```ts
changeMark(change: "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed" | "unchanged" | { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged" }): { "data-change"?: "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed" }
```

The standard change marking for one item of a diff view: `data-change`
with the item's change (`added`, `removed`, `modified` or `renamed`), and
nothing for an unchanged one. The kit's styles draw a marked HTML
`pk-region` as a fill with a same-hue edge, and a marked SVG item's
`pk-diff-shape` (its card or circle) the same way; removed items are
dashed and their `pk-diff-text` struck through. Spread it on the element
that carries `data-entity-id`.

### `changesScope`

```ts
changesScope(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction> | undefined, filter: FilterPayload | undefined): ChangesScope | undefined
```

The Changes scope a renderer presents, or undefined when the host shows every item (or this is one extraction). The
host's filter `scope` is what it shows, its changes and their context, each change with every row presenting it (a
split's parts): the summary filter and find recede what they leave out (`ids`), never narrowing what is laid out. A
host before `scope` sent it in `ids`. Past the filter's ID limit, or before the host says, the kit reads the same
from the comparison's change context, or derives it from the structure for a comparison saved without context
(`changeContext`).

### `ChangesScope`

```ts
interface ChangesScope
```

What a Changes scope shows: the changes it is about and the unchanged items that give them context.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `changes` | `"changes": ReadonlySet<string>` | The change rows in scope, by row ID. |
| `context` | `"context": ReadonlySet<string>` | The unchanged rows shown to read them: their relationships' endpoints and the items that contain them. |
| `shown` | `"shown": ReadonlySet<string>` | Both: every row the scope shows. |

### `clampZoom`

```ts
clampZoom(value: number, fit: number): number
```

`value` within 1 (fitted) and `maxZoom(fit)`, rounded to a millionth so stepping back lands exactly.

### `classifyChange`

```ts
classifyChange(change: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }): "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed" | "unchanged"
```

The one change a row presents: its status, except that a renamed row whose content is unchanged is `renamed`. A
renamed and otherwise changed row keeps its status (see `describeChange` and `statusParts` for both).

### `cleanPolyline`

```ts
cleanPolyline(polyline: Array<Point>): Array<Point>
```

A polyline without repeated points and with collinear runs merged.

### `codeStatisticsControls`

```ts
codeStatisticsControls: readonly [{ "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": "blank" | "code" | "comment" | "files" | "lines" }>; "default": "blank" | "code" | "comment" | "files" | "lines"; "description": "What each language row counts"; "group": "statistics"; "groupLabel": "Statistics"; "id": "measure"; "label": "Measure"; "type": "choice" }, { "default": false | true; "description": "One row per language, or the code, comment and blank composition"; "group": "statistics"; "groupLabel": "Statistics"; "id": "byLanguage"; "label": "By language"; "type": "toggle" }, { "choices": [{ "label": "Bars"; "value": "bars" }, { "label": "Share"; "value": "share" }, { "label": "Table"; "value": "table" }]; "default": "bars" | "share" | "table"; "group": "statistics"; "groupLabel": "Statistics"; "id": "chart"; "label": "Chart"; "type": "choice" }]
```

### `codeStatisticsControlsFor`

```ts
codeStatisticsControlsFor(entities: Iterable<Entity | undefined, any, any>): Array<ControlBase & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } | ControlBase & { "default": false | true; "type": "toggle" } | ControlBase & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } | ControlBase & { "icon"?: "collapse" | "download" | "expand" | "filter" | "fit" | "next" | "previous" | "reset" | "search" | "settings" | "zoom-in" | "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>
```

The code-statistics controls for these entities: the scope control joins when they carry test counts. Generic
measurements (`genericMetrics`: values without line or file counts) have one value per row, so only the chart is offered.

### `ColorTokenName`

```ts
type ColorTokenName = "accent" | "accent-emphasis" | "accent-muted" | "added" | "added-border" | "added-emphasis" | "added-highlight" | "added-muted" | "bg" | "bg-inset" | "bg-overlay" | "bg-subtle" | "border" | "border-emphasis" | "border-muted" | "divider" | "fg" | "fg-muted" | "fg-on-emphasis" | "fg-subtle" | "focus" | "highlight" | "modified" | "modified-border" | "modified-emphasis" | "modified-highlight" | "modified-muted" | "moved" | "moved-border" | "moved-emphasis" | "moved-highlight" | "moved-muted" | "removed" | "removed-border" | "removed-emphasis" | "removed-highlight" | "removed-muted" | "surface-canvas" | "surface-header" | "surface-inset" | "surface-raised"
```

Color token names without `color-`, such as `fg-muted` or `added-border`.

### `columnGap`

```ts
columnGap: number
```

Space between columns on the grid a top-to-bottom layout's cards snap to (see `columnGrid`): a channel for a route between two cards, clear
of both (`edgeNodeSpacing` each side), with room to spare, so columns read apart and a relationship can pass
between them.

### `ColumnSort`

```ts
type ColumnSort<T> = "number" | "string" | false | { (a: T, b: T): number }
```

How a column orders its rows: `number` and `string` compare its `value` (strings naturally, so `v2` comes before
`v10`), a function compares two versions of rows itself, and `false` makes the column unsortable. Without it a
column with a `value` sorts as a string, or as a number when the values are numbers.

### `compareIds`

```ts
compareIds(left: string, right: string): number
```

Code-unit order, the same order the Engine uses for IDs.

### `comparisonModel`

```ts
comparisonModel<X extends Extraction>(before: X, after: X, comparison: Comparison): ComparisonModel<X>
```

Presents a comparison of `before` and `after` as a model, pairing their items exactly as `comparison` says (see
`presentComparison`) and resolving its steps to rows.

### `ComparisonModel`

```ts
interface ComparisonModel<X extends Extraction = Extraction>
```

An extraction or comparison resolved for presentation. Identity comes only
from the comparison (`presentComparison` in the SDK); nothing is matched,
normalized or inferred here. In extraction mode `before` and `after` are the
same extraction and every row is unchanged.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after": X` | The After extraction; the extraction itself in extraction mode. |
| `before` | `"before": X` | The Before extraction; the extraction itself in extraction mode. |
| `changeRows` | `"changeRows"?: ReadonlyMap<string, Array<string>>` | The presented rows of each comparison change with more than one item: a split's further parts and a merge's further sources are rows of their own, while the host names the change by its ID alone. |
| `entities` | `"entities": Array<EntityChange<X["entities"][number]>>` | One row per entity across both extractions, its Before and After versions paired by the comparison. |
| `entityRow` | `"entityRow": { "after": ReadonlyMap<string, string>; "before": ReadonlyMap<string, string> }` | Maps an entity ID of either extraction to the presented row that shows it. |
| `mode` | `"mode": "comparison" \| "extraction"` | Whether this presents one extraction or a comparison of two. |
| `relationships` | `"relationships": Array<EntityChange<X["relationships"][number]>>` | One row per relationship across both extractions, paired like `entities`. |
| `reverse` | `"reverse": "explicit" \| "mirror"` | How playing backward orders steps: the forward steps reversed, or `reverseSteps`. |
| `reverseSteps` | `"reverseSteps"?: Array<PresentedStep>` | Backward presentation order (first presented when leaving progress 1) when `reverse` is `explicit`. |
| `schema` | `"schema": string` | The extraction's domain schema; a comparison's is After's. |
| `steps` | `"steps": Array<PresentedStep>` | Steps in forward presentation order. |

### `compileTimeline`

```ts
compileTimeline<T>(steps: Array<T>, options?: undefined | { "lead"?: { (step: T): false | true }; "tail"?: { (step: T): false | true } }): Array<T & { "hold": number; "lead": number; "radius": number; "tail": number; "time": number }>
```

Turns ordered steps into windows on [0, 1], separated by holds. Comparisons
carry order and grouping only; this presentation timing is the renderer's.
Each step's slot is `gap` wide: its motion window takes `1 - stepHoldShare`
of the slot and the rest is a hold shared with its neighbour, so no step
begins before the previous one has finished and settled. A step `lead`
accepts gets a reading lead of `readingShare` slots before its motion, and
one `tail` accepts a reading tail as long after it. Positions depend only
on the sequence and are centred on the midpoint, so reversing a sequence
mirrors its timeline exactly.

### `ContentBox`

```ts
interface ContentBox
```

A box in content units, by its top-left corner.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `"height": number` | The box's height. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The box's width. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | The box's left side. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | The box's top side. |

### `contentHeightCap`

```ts
contentHeightCap(token: string | undefined, viewport: undefined | { "height": number }): number | undefined
```

The most a content-sized frame whose content pans and zooms asks for, CSS px, from the host's optional
`stage-max-height` theme token: a length in `px`, or in `vh` of the host window's height (`viewport`, as the host
reports it), at least `contentMinimumCap`. Undefined when the host sends no such token (the frame takes the
content's height, uncapped) or a `vh` value before the host has reported its viewport. A host that lays the frame in
its scrolling page sends it, so a canvas no taller than the window can be seen whole, and panned, without scrolling
the page; content taller than that at the opening scale is fitted to the capped stage, or opens at the floor and pans.

### `contentMinimumCap`

```ts
contentMinimumCap: 360
```

The least a content-sized stage that pans and zooms is capped at, CSS px, however short the window.

### `contentStart`

```ts
contentStart(boxes: Array<ContentBox>, bounds: ContentBox, inset?: number | { "top"?: number; "x": number; "y": number }, margin?: number, align?: "centre" | "left", clear?: number): { (view: { "height"?: number; "scale": number; "width"?: number }): { "left": number; "top": number } }
```

The reading start of content whose bounds are `bounds` (content units), drawn after `inset` CSS px of padding (or
`{x, y}`, across and down, with `top` above the content when it differs from `y`):
the scroll offsets that put the content's top row of boxes (those whose top is within the smallest box's height
of the topmost) at the viewport's top left, from its leftmost box, `margin` units clear of it. So content whose
bounds start with empty room (a wide layout whose top row is at the right) opens on cards, never on empty
canvas. It depends only on the boxes, the scale and the viewport's size, never on highlighting, and the view is
placed again as a frame settles to its height. The scroll range clamps it where the content ends.

Its left edge runs between boxes, never through one, counting the boxes the viewport reaches (by its height when
given) that hold no other (cards, not the groups around them): where it would cut one, it moves to the nearest edge,
`margin` clear of a box and within the scroll range, that cuts none and keeps the top row's leftmost box whole in
view (by the viewport's width), else at least that box's left side; where there is none, the start is the
drawing's own left side.

`align: 'centre'` puts the top row's horizontal middle at the viewport's instead, for a layout that reads from its
top row outward (a graph laid out top to bottom), so the row is cut evenly on both sides even when it sits to one
side of the content (cards placed beside it, or another moment of a transition, widen the bounds). A row too wide
for the viewport opens from its leftmost box instead, as `'left'` does, never cut at the left.

`clear` keeps that many more CSS px clear at the view's left, beside `margin`, reaching into the padding: content
drawn flush with a host's stage inset (`inset.x` and `clear` the same) opens with its leftmost box that inset from
the view's edge, on the host's column.

### `ContextPaths`

```ts
interface ContextPaths
```

Which relationships `followContext` follows, by kind: to an item's sources (`incoming`), or its targets (`outgoing`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `incoming` | `"incoming"?: { (kind: string): false \| true }` | Follow a relationship of this kind from its target back to its source (a dependency to the package that needs it). |
| `outgoing` | `"outgoing"?: { (kind: string): false \| true }` | Follow a relationship of this kind from its source to its target (a probe to the hook it attaches to). |

### `countText`

```ts
countText(count: number, singular: string, plural?: string, locale?: string | undefined): string
```

`count` and its noun, in the locale's digits: `1 package`, `3 packages`.

### `coveredBottom`

```ts
coveredBottom(input: { "cover": Array<CoverRect>; "maxScale"?: number; "origin"?: { "x": number; "y": number }; "padding"?: FitPadding | number; "size": { "height": number; "width": number }; "view": { "height": number; "width": number } }): number
```

The space a fitted drawing keeps below it, CSS px, as `coveredTop` keeps above: clear of what the host overlays at
the stage's foot (the rectangles below its middle, such as a floating legend and summary), only where the fitted
drawing would reach them; else the padding's own bottom (`y`).

### `coveredPadding`

```ts
coveredPadding(input: { "cover": Array<CoverRect>; "maxScale"?: number; "origin"?: { "x": number; "y": number }; "padding"?: FitPadding | number; "size": { "height": number; "width": number }; "view": { "height": number; "width": number } }): { "top": number; "y": number }
```

The top and bottom (`y`) a fitted drawing keeps from the host's covers at both ends (`coveredTop`, `coveredBottom`),
resolved together: moving one edge refits and recentres the drawing, which can then reach the other end's cover, so
each is raised until the fit clears both (only ever raised, so it settles in a few steps).

### `coveredTop`

```ts
coveredTop(input: { "cover": Array<CoverRect>; "maxScale"?: number; "origin"?: { "x": number; "y": number }; "padding"?: FitPadding | number; "size": { "height": number; "width": number }; "view": { "height": number; "width": number } }): number
```

The space a fitted drawing keeps above it, CSS px, so it never opens under what the host overlays at the stage's
top (`cover`, the rectangles above its middle): the drawing is fitted with `padding` and centred in a stage of
`view` whose top left is `origin` in the frame, as `useFitScale` and a `margin: auto` drawing place it. Where that
leaves it clear of every rectangle (a flat graph centred well below a chip), the padding's own top; else the top
that clears the lowest rectangle it reaches, by `coverGap`. Decided from the drawing's fit without the cover, never
from the result, so it can't oscillate. The drawing still pans under the cover once zoomed.

### `coverGap`

```ts
coverGap: 8
```

The space kept between a fitted drawing and a cover above it, CSS px.

### `CoverRect`

```ts
interface CoverRect
```

A rectangle of the frame the host overlays (its `stage-cover` theme token), CSS px from the frame's top left.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `"height": number` | Its height, CSS px. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | Its width, CSS px. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | Its left edge, CSS px from the frame's left. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | Its top edge, CSS px from the frame's top. |

### `createGraphTransition`

```ts
createGraphTransition(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction>, schedule: Array<ScheduledStep>, options?: GraphTransitionOptions): Promise<GraphTransition>
```

Lays out a comparison's staged graph transition (see `GraphTransition`): the union of both revisions and each
revision's own layout, with ELK, up front. The result is a pure function of progress, cheap enough to call every
frame. An extraction has one layout, so every frame is the same. `schedule` is the comparison's scheduled steps
(`RendererProps.schedule`); rows no step places arrive and leave in the unscheduled window.

### `createModel`

```ts
createModel<X extends Extraction>(init: RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": X; "before": X; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } | RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": X; "mode": "extraction" }): ComparisonModel<X>
```

Presents an extraction (one state) or a comparison (two states) from the host's `init`.

### `createStagedTimeline`

```ts
createStagedTimeline(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction>, schedule: Array<ScheduledStep>, options?: { "include"?: ReadonlySet<string> }): StagedTimeline
```

Step-driven staging for renderers that interpolate between their own
layouts (trees, circle packings, lists). Compute one layout per stage, then draw
a frame by interpolating `stages[from]` to `stages[to]` by `mix`. Only one
step's move window is ever active, so layouts are never blended three ways.

```ts
cubicPoint(p0: Point, c1: Point, c2: Point, p1: Point, t: number): Point
```

The point at `t` on one segment `[p0, c1, c2, p1]`.

```ts
current<T>(change: EntityChange<T>, progress: number): T
```

The version of a row a viewer should read at this point: before until halfway, then after.

```ts
cutText(text: string, room: number): string
```

```ts
defaultBorderWidths: BorderWidths
```

### `describeChange`

```ts
describeChange(change: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }): string
```

A change in words for titles and accessible names: its label, or both for a renamed and changed row.

```ts
detailText(text: string): string
```

### `DiffCardInput`

```ts
interface DiffCardInput
```

What `diffCardText` lays out: an entity row's two versions and the renderer's card text for it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after"?: Entity \| undefined` | The entity in the After revision; its kind is drawn, else Before's, and a changed label shows both. |
| `before` | `"before"?: Entity \| undefined` | The entity in the Before revision; at least one of `before` and `after` must be given. |
| `detail` | `"detail"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): string \| undefined }` | A short identifier at the right of the kind line, per revision (see `GraphCanvasProps.detail`). |
| `fields` | `"fields"?: Array<FieldLine> \| undefined` | Field changes drawn under the label (see `GraphCanvasProps.changedFields`), at most `fieldLineLimit`. |
| `icon` | `"icon"?: false \| true \| undefined` | Whether the card shows an icon before its kind line (see `GraphCanvasProps.icon`), which its kind line makes room for. |
| `kind` | `"kind"?: undefined \| { "identifier"?: false \| true; "note"?: string; "text": string }` | The card's kind line (see `GraphCanvasProps.kindLine`); the entity's kind otherwise. |
| `prose` | `"prose"?: false \| true` | The label is human language, drawn in sans. |
| `reserve` | `"reserve"?: number \| undefined` | Room kept free at the right of the kind line, for an expander (see `EntityCard`). |
| `status` | `"status"?: Array<StatusPart> \| undefined` | The parts of the card's status footer (see `SvgChangeStatus`), which the card is wide enough to hold. |
| `textScale` | `"textScale"?: number \| undefined` | The theme's extra-small type size over the default 12 (see `GraphCardText.textScale`). |
| `width` | `"width"?: number \| undefined` | The card's width, when the graph's cards share one (at least what this card's text needs on one line, see `DiffCardText.width`); by default the card's own. |

### `DiffCardLine`

```ts
interface DiffCardLine
```

One line of a diff card's text: an SVG `<text>` at (`x`, `y`) made of styled spans.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `anchor` | `"anchor"?: "end"` | `end` for a line aligned to the card's right (a detail beside the kind line); starts at `x` otherwise. |
| `className` | `"className": string` | The line's role, for its style: `node-kind`, `node-label`, `node-detail`, `node-field-key` or `node-field-value`. |
| `identifier` | `"identifier": false \| true` | Drawn in the monospace font (an identifier or value). |
| `spans` | `"spans": Array<DiffCardSpan>` | The line's text in runs, each in its own tone. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | Where the line starts, from the card's left side; where it ends when `anchor` is `end`. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | Text baseline, from the card's top. |

### `diffCardMetrics`

```ts
diffCardMetrics: { "bottom": 15; "charWidth": 7.4; "fieldGap": 2; "fieldLineLimit": 3; "fieldsGap": 6; "fileTextLeft": 40; "firstBaseline": 21; "labelGap": 6; "line": 14; "proseCharWidth": 6.6; "textInset": 16; "textLeft": 16; "valueLineLimit": 6 }
```

Card geometry in card units: text runs from `textLeft` (`fileTextLeft` on a file card, after its icon) to
`textInset` before the card's right side. Advances are at the type scale's default size (12): `textScale` scales them.

### `DiffCardSpan`

```ts
interface DiffCardSpan
```

A run of a diff card line's text in one tone.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | `"text": string` | The text, verbatim. |
| `tone` | `"tone"?: "arrow" \| "note" \| "now" \| "was"` | `was` (struck, removed hue), `now` (added hue), `arrow` or `note` (muted sans). |

### `diffCardText`

```ts
diffCardText(input: DiffCardInput): DiffCardText
```

Lays out a diff card's text (see `DiffCardText`). Deterministic: the same entities always give the same lines.

### `DiffCardText`

```ts
interface DiffCardText
```

A graph card's text in diff mode, laid out whole: nothing is cut off with an
ellipsis. The card is as wide as its longest line needs, up to the widest
card (`cardWidthRange`); longer names, types, versions and field values wrap
onto more lines (breaking after `_ . / - , :` first, see `wrapText`) and the
card grows to hold them; the union layout places the taller cards. Positions
are in card units from the card's top-left corner.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `"height": number` | The card's height: its kind's own height, or taller for its text, footer included. |
| `lines` | `"lines": Array<DiffCardLine>` | Every line of text, top to bottom, each at its own position: draw them as they are (see `DiffCardLines`). |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The card's width: what its text needs on one line, within `cardWidthRange`. |

### `DiffCounts`

```ts
type DiffCounts = { unchanged: number; added: number; removed: number; modified: number; renamed: number; }
```

How many items have each change, every classification present (zero when none).

### `DiffEntity`

```ts
interface DiffEntity
```

One entity of a diff view: its row, its change and, when it is on both sides, what differs.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after"?: Entity` | The After version; absent for a removed entity. |
| `before` | `"before"?: Entity` | The Before version; absent for an added entity. |
| `change` | `"change": "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "renamed" \| "unchanged"` | The row's change, from `classifyChange`. |
| `entity` | `"entity": Entity` | The version to draw: After when it exists, otherwise Before (a removed entity stays as it was). |
| `fields` | `"fields": Array<FieldChange>` | What differs between the two versions, label first, then `data` fields by name; empty unless both exist. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The comparison's entity row ID, which the host selects by (`data-entity-id`). |
| `row` | `"row": EntityChange<Entity>` | The comparison's row, both versions included. |

### `diffModel`

```ts
diffModel(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction>): DiffModel
```

The union of a comparison for diff mode (see `DiffModel`). In extraction
mode every row is unchanged. Entity order is the model's; relationship
parts follow their relationship's order, the old part first.

### `DiffModel`

```ts
interface DiffModel
```

Diff mode's data: the union of both revisions, every entity and
relationship once, each with the change the comparison gave it and, for
one present on both sides, what differs between its two versions. A diff
view lays out this union once, in the renderer's own visual form, and
marks each item with its change in place (see `changeMark`). Identity and
status come only from the comparison; nothing is matched or inferred here.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `counts` | `"counts": { "entities": DiffCounts; "relationships": DiffCounts }` | How many entities and relationships have each change; a rewired relationship counts once, as its row's change. |
| `entities` | `"entities": Array<DiffEntity>` | Every entity row once, in the comparison's order. |
| `entity` | `"entity"(id: string): DiffEntity \| undefined` | The entity on an entity row ID of the comparison. |
| `relationships` | `"relationships": Array<DiffRelationship>` | Drawn relationships: one per relationship, or two for one rewired between other endpoints (its old part removed, its new part added). |

### `DiffRelationship`

```ts
interface DiffRelationship
```

One drawn relationship of a diff view. A relationship whose endpoints are the same entity rows in both revisions
is one part; one rewired between other rows is two, its old part removed and its new part added. A relationship
whose endpoint has no entity row is not drawn.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `change` | `"change": "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "renamed" \| "unchanged"` | This part's change: a rewired relationship's old part is removed and its new part added. |
| `from` | `"from": string` | Entity row ID of the source endpoint. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The comparison's relationship row ID, shared by both parts of a rewired relationship. |
| `key` | `"key": string` | Unique per drawn part: the relationship ID, or `<id>:before` and `<id>:after` for a rewired one (the graph layout's route keys). |
| `relationship` | `"relationship": Relationship` | This part's relationship: After's for a part on both sides or the new part, Before's for the old part. |
| `row` | `"row": EntityChange<Relationship>` | The comparison's relationship row. |
| `side` | `"side": "after" \| "before" \| "both"` | Which revision this part belongs to: both, or only one for an added, removed or rewired part. |
| `to` | `"to": string` | Entity row ID of the target endpoint. |

### `DirectionLatch`

```ts
class DirectionLatch
```

Chooses which schedule a renderer presents. Under `mirror` order there is
only one. Under `explicit` order the schedule latches to the direction of
travel when progress leaves an endpoint and keeps it until progress reaches
an endpoint again, so reversing mid-transition never jumps to another
timeline. Keep one latch per document.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `constructor` | `new (): DirectionLatch` |  |
| `update` | `"update"(progress: number, direction: -1 \| 1): -1 \| 1` | The direction to present at `progress`, given the current playback `direction`: `1` at progress 0 or below, `-1` at 1 or above, and in between the direction latched when progress left an endpoint (`direction` if it hasn't). |

### `domainIndex`

```ts
domainIndex(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction>): Omit<DomainIndex, "visible">
```

Entity and relationship rows keyed by identity, with relationships resolved to entity rows.

### `DomainIndex`

```ts
interface DomainIndex
```

A comparison indexed for domain renderers (from `useDomainIndex`): rows keyed by identity, and relationship rows
resolved to the entity rows they join, through whichever revision has the relationship (the later one when both do).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `changeOf` | `"changeOf": Map<string, EntityChange<Entity>>` | Maps an entity ID of either extraction to its row. |
| `changes` | `"changes": Array<EntityChange<Entity>>` | Every entity row. |
| `edges` | `"edges": Array<EntityChange<Relationship>>` | Relationship rows from both extractions, so a dropped relationship still animates out. |
| `into` | `"into": Map<string, Array<EntityChange<Relationship>>>` | Relationships arriving at each entity row, keyed by entity row ID; a row with none has no key. |
| `out` | `"out": Map<string, Array<EntityChange<Relationship>>>` | Relationships leaving each entity row, keyed by entity row ID; a row with none has no key. |
| `visible` | `"visible": Array<EntityChange<Entity>>` | Rows a viewer can currently see: included and present at this progress. |

### `dotGrid`

```ts
dotGrid(scale: number, origin: { "x": number; "y": number }, spacing?: { "fade": { "from": number; "to": number }; "units": number }): DotGrid
```

The dot grid for content drawn at `scale` whose content-unit origin is `origin` CSS px into its scroll container's
scrollable area, so the dots stay put on the content: they pan with it (the grid scrolls with the content) and keep
their place on it as it zooms.

### `DotGrid`

```ts
interface DotGrid
```

Where and how strongly to draw the dot grid at one zoom (`dotGrid`'s result), as CSS for the scroll container's
`background-size`, `background-position` and grid opacity.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `opacity` | `"opacity": number` | 0 (hidden) to 1. |
| `spacing` | `"spacing": number` | CSS px between dots. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | The grid's horizontal offset in the scroll container's content, CSS px, within one spacing: a dot is at each multiple from it. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | Its vertical offset, likewise. |

### `dotGridSpacing`

```ts
dotGridSpacing: { "fade": { "from": number; "to": number }; "units": number }
```

The dot grid behind zoomable content (the kit's `pk-dot-grid` class on the scroll container): a dot every `units`
content units, so it is drawn `units * scale` CSS px apart and moves with the content as it pans and zooms; it fades

### `drawnEdge`

```ts
drawnEdge(edge: Pick<TransitionEdge, "points">, from: TransitionNode, to: TransitionNode, outset?: number): { "base": Point; "d": string; "direction": Point; "head": string; "tip": Point }
```

A relationship as drawn: its route with each end on its card's face at the
card's current scale, and the kit's arrowhead (see `arrowHead`) with its tip
on the target card's face, the shaft running straight into the middle of
its base.

### `ease`

```ts
ease(value: number): number
```

The kit's shared ease for anything a renderer interpolates from progress
(sizes, counts, angles, positions): the same quintic smootherstep graph
layouts move on, so every renderer starts and stops softly and a reversed
comparison draws the same frames. Ease the value, then round it for display.

### `easeIn`

```ts
easeIn(value: number): number
```

Cubic ease-in, the mirror of `easeOut`: gentle to start, quick to finish. Fade-outs use it.

### `easeOut`

```ts
easeOut(value: number): number
```

Cubic ease-out: quick to start, gentle to arrive. Fade-ins use it.

### `easeWithin`

```ts
easeWithin(progress: number, start: number, end: number): number
```

`ease` applied to progress through `[start, end]`: 0 before the window, 1 after it.

### `edgeArrowHeadLength`

```ts
edgeArrowHeadLength: 8.5
```

The arrowhead's length from tip to base (see `arrowHeadLength`); paths from `boxEdge` end this far short of the card.

### `edgeKind`

```ts
edgeKind(edge: EntityChange<Relationship>): string
```

A relationship row's kind: After's, or Before's for a removed relationship.

### `edgeMarkerId`

```ts
edgeMarkerId(prefix: string, key: string): string
```

A document-unique marker ID for an arbitrary key, safe in `url(#…)`.

### `edgePaint`

```ts
edgePaint(change: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }, emphasis: number, weight: number, base?: string): { "stroke": string; "strokeWidth": string }
```

Explicit stroke paint for a relationship, blended toward its change color by
emphasis. `weight` is the line's weight relative to the host's border width
(the kit's `--stroke`); emphasis thickens it toward the thick border width.
`base` is its paint without emphasis (the kit's edge color by default).

### `edgePresence`

```ts
edgePresence(edge: EntityChange<Relationship>, progress: number): number
```

Whether a relationship is present at this point, so lists match the timeline.

### `EdgeTurn`

```ts
interface EdgeTurn
```

One S a downward `boxEdge` arrow turns on, as `routeTracks` takes it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `axis` | `"axis": Point` | The unit direction the S leaves and arrives along: down, for `boxEdge`'s downward arrows. |
| `band` | `"band": readonly [number, number]` | Where along `axis` the S may turn, as distances from `start`. |
| `end` | `"end": Point` | Where the S ends: the arrow's tip for its last S. |
| `lead` | `"lead": false \| true` | Whether the S ends with the arrowhead's lead-in: true for the S into the target, false for one into a corridor. |
| `start` | `"start": Point` | Where the S starts: the arrow's start for its first S. |

### `emphasisInset`

```ts
emphasisInset(widths?: BorderWidths): number
```

How far a change border (`strong`) is inset from the card's box, so its outer edge is the plain border's.

### `EmphasisOf`

```ts
type EmphasisOf = { (change: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined } & { "id"?: string }, id?: string | undefined): number }
```

Step-scoped emphasis for one row: pass the row, and its row ID when the row object has none.

### `emphasisRise`

```ts
emphasisRise(step: Pick<ScheduledStep, "radius" | "time"> & Partial<Pick<ScheduledStep, "lead" | "tail" | "travel">> | undefined, progress: number): number
```

How much of the host's change highlighting a change in `step` shows at
`progress`: 0 until the step's window begins in the direction the schedule
is travelled (`travel`), then rising (over the first fifth of the reading
part travel enters, else over the start of the motion) to 1, where it stays
until the host's own endpoint fade. Earlier steps never pre-tint later
changes, and an explicit reverse order mirrors it. A change no step places
shows the host's highlighting unscaled.

### `entityKindLine`

```ts
entityKindLine(kind: string): KindLineText
```

An entity kind as a card shows it when the renderer gives no kind line of its own. A plain word or phrase
(`resource`, `data-source`, `message_queue`) is a category, so it reads as a label in sentence case ("Resource",
"Data source", and "npm package", whose name is lowercase; see `sentenceCase`); anything code-like (dots, slashes,
colons, inner capitals, digits) is data, shown verbatim in mono.

### `entityPresence`

```ts
entityPresence(change: EntityChange<unknown>, progress: number): number
```

Linear presence for renderers without staged timing: arrivals fade in, departures out.

### `extractionModel`

```ts
extractionModel<X extends Extraction>(extraction: X): ComparisonModel<X>
```

Presents one extraction as a model: every entity and relationship is a row with itself on both sides, unchanged,
and there are no steps.

### `FaceBox`

```ts
interface FaceBox
```

A card's box, in the route's coordinates.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `"height": number` | The box's height. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The box's width. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | The box's left side. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | The box's top side. |

### `fadeIn`

```ts
fadeIn(progress: number, center: number, radius: number): number
```

Presence of something fading in over `[center - radius, center + radius]`: eased out, so it arrives softly.

### `fadeOut`

```ts
fadeOut(progress: number, center: number, radius: number): number
```

Presence of something fading out over the window: eased in, so it leaves
softly. The exact mirror of `fadeIn`, so a reversed comparison draws the same frames.

### `FieldChange`

```ts
interface FieldChange
```

One field that differs between two versions of an entity (see `fieldChanges`); values are as extracted.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after": unknown` | The field's value in After; `undefined` when that version lacks the `data` field. |
| `before` | `"before": unknown` | The field's value in Before; `undefined` when that version lacks the `data` field. |
| `key` | `"key": string` | `label`, `kind`, `confidence` or a `data` field's name. |

### `fieldChanges`

```ts
fieldChanges(before: Entity | undefined, after: Entity | undefined, options?: { "fields"?: Array<string> }): Array<FieldChange>
```

What differs between two versions of an entity: its label, kind and
confidence, then each `data` field (by name, so the order is stable). Pass
`fields` to compare only those `data` fields, in that order.

### `FieldLine`

```ts
interface FieldLine
```

One field change as text, for drawing inline (see `ValueChange` and GraphCanvas `changedFields`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after": string` | The After value as written (`formatValue`): `null` when absent. |
| `before` | `"before": string` | The Before value as written (`formatValue`): `null` when absent. |
| `key` | `"key": string` | The field's name, or a leaf's path within an object field (`hardwareProfile.vmSize`, `ingress[0].from_port`). |
| `prose` | `"prose"?: true` | `key` is in plain words (`test tokens`), drawn as human text rather than as the field's identifier. |
| `summary` | `"summary"?: true` | The line only says something changed, in words (`key`, such as `2 other fields changed`), without values: for changes too bulky for a card, which the host's details show. |

### `fieldLines`

```ts
fieldLines(row: EntityChange<Entity>, options?: { "exclude"?: Array<string>; "fields"?: Array<string>; "object"?: string }): Array<FieldLine>
```

Field changes between two versions as text lines (see `fieldChanges`),
`data` fields only unless `fields` names others; values verbatim
(`formatValue`). Pass `object` to compare the fields of one object-valued
`data` field instead, such as a resource's `values`, down to the leaves
that changed (see `leafChanges`), so a nested setting reads as its own path
(`properties.hardwareProfile.vmSize`) rather than the whole object twice.

### `fileCategory`

```ts
fileCategory(path: string): Category
```

The category of a repository path: its Linguist language, else its extension.

### `Fit`

```ts
interface Fit
```

The fit `useFitScale` measured: the content's scale and the stage's inner size.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `"height": number` | The stage's inner height, CSS px; 0 until measured. |
| `scale` | `"scale": number` | Scale from content units to CSS px at which all of the content fits the stage; 0 until the stage has been measured. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The stage's inner width, CSS px; 0 until measured. |

### `FitOptions`

```ts
interface FitOptions
```

How `useFitScale` fits content to its stage.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `aspect` | `"aspect"?: number` | The shape (width / height) to report for arranging held panes, when the view opens on part of the content (see `StageZoomOptions.opening`) rather than all of it; default the content's own. |
| `drawnScale` | `"drawnScale"?: number` | The scale the content is drawn at now (see `useStageZoom`). Zoomed in past where it opens, a content-sized host is asked for the height it takes at that scale, up to its `stage-max-height`, so the stage grows into the page before it pans; the fit itself never depends on it. |
| `floor` | `"floor"?: number` | The scale at which the content's smallest text reaches the kit's `openingFloorPx` (see `useOpeningFloor`; pass the same to `useStageZoom`). When fitting the width draws text smaller, a content-sized host is asked for the height the content takes at that floor, where it opens, so the opening view pans only sideways. |
| `maxScale` | `"maxScale"?: number` | Largest scale (default 1: small content is centred at its own size, never enlarged). |
| `minHeight` | `"minHeight"?: number` | Smallest stage height to ask a content-sized host for, CSS px (default 200), unless the content is scaled down to its width. |
| `padding` | `"padding"?: FitPadding \| number` | Space kept around the content inside the stage, CSS px (default 16), or apart across (`x`) and down (`y`). |

### `fitPadding`

```ts
fitPadding(padding?: FitPadding | number): FitPadding
```

`padding` across and down.

### `FitPadding`

```ts
interface FitPadding
```

Space around fitted content, CSS px: across (each side, left and right) and down (top and bottom).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `top` | `"top"?: number` | Space above the content, CSS px, when it differs from `y` (a host's `stage-inset-top`); `y` stays below it. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | Space at the content's left and at its right, CSS px. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | Space above the content and below it, CSS px. |

### `fitPaddingDown`

```ts
fitPaddingDown(padding?: FitPadding | number): { "top": number; "total": number }
```

The space `padding` keeps above the content and the space it keeps above and below together, CSS px.

### `fitScale`

```ts
fitScale(size: { "height": number; "width": number }, stage: { "height": number; "width": number }, __2?: Pick<FitOptions, "maxScale" | "padding">): { "scale": number; "widthFirst": number }
```

The scale at which content of `size` fits a stage of `stage` (CSS px) with `padding` around it, in both
dimensions and never above `maxScale`, and the scale that fits only its width, which a content-sized host's
preferred height is measured at.

### `focusedIds`

```ts
focusedIds(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction> | undefined, focus: RendererFocus | undefined, diff: false | true): Set<string> | undefined
```

The selection IDs a focus request names, in a model: its item, or every changed entity and relationship. Undefined
when it names none (`all`, or no request); in diff mode without a request, the changes.

### `Folded`

```ts
type Folded<T> = { "item": T; "type": "item" } | { "items": Array<T>; "key": string; "open"?: false | true; "type": "fold" }
```

One entry of a folded list: an item it shows, or a fold standing for a run of items it doesn't. An `open` fold's items
follow it, and it is the way to fold them again.

### `foldList`

```ts
foldList<T>(items: Array<T>, idOf: { (item: T): string }, shown: ReadonlySet<string> | undefined, expanded?: ReadonlySet<string>): Array<{ "item": T; "type": "item" } | { "items": Array<T>; "key": string; "open"?: false | true; "type": "fold" }>
```

A list with every run of items `shown` leaves out folded into one entry, keyed by its first item; a run `expanded`
names is listed after its fold, `open`. A run of one item stays, as its fold would take as much room. Every item is shown when `shown` is
undefined. Fold the union of a comparison (or each pane's list in the union's order) so both revisions fold alike.

### `foldPrefix`

```ts
foldPrefix: "pk-fold:"
```

The ID prefix of a fold `scopedModel` adds: `pk-fold:` and the row ID of the entity whose parts it stands for.

### `followContext`

```ts
followContext(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction>, changes: ReadonlySet<string>, paths: ContextPaths): Set<string>
```

The rows that place a comparison's changes along the relationships `paths` names, transitively: from each changed
entity and each end of a changed relationship, in whichever revision has them, every entity reached and the
relationships followed to it. For example a changed package's dependents up to the workspace, or a changed selector's
probe, the probe's policy and the hook it attaches to.

### `followEndpoints`

```ts
followEndpoints(points: Array<Point>, source: Point, target: Point): Array<Point>
```

Moves a chain with its endpoints: each control point follows the source
and target displacement in proportion to its place along the chain, so the
route stays attached while its cards move.

### `FontSizeStep`

```ts
type FontSizeStep = "lg" | "md" | "sm" | "xl" | "xs"
```

Steps of the type scale: `xs` (12px) to `xl` (20px); `md` is the body size, the `font-size` token.

### `FontWeightStep`

```ts
type FontWeightStep = "bold" | "medium" | "normal" | "semibold"
```

Font weights: `normal` (400), `medium` (500), `semibold` (600) and `bold` (700).

### `formatValue`

```ts
formatValue(value: unknown): string
```

An extracted value as it is written: strings as they are, everything else as JSON, and an absent value as `null`.

### `gappedBend`

```ts
gappedBend(start: Point, end: Point, axis: Point, from: number, to: number, options?: RouteOptions): Array<Point> | undefined
```

The S confined to `[from, to]` along the axis (distances from `start`):
straight stubs outside it. Used to fit an S through the gap between two
rows of cards when a full-height one would cross a card.

### `GraphAlignment`

```ts
type GraphAlignment = "BALANCED" | "LEFTDOWN" | "LEFTUP" | "RIGHTDOWN" | "RIGHTUP"
```

How a layout placed its cards: one of the four Brandes–Köpf alignments (`LEFTUP`, `RIGHTUP`, `LEFTDOWN`,
`RIGHTDOWN`), with one port in the middle of each card face, or their `BALANCED` average with ELK's own ports.

### `graphCardsWidth`

```ts
graphCardsWidth(rows: Array<EntityChange<Entity>>, text?: GraphCardText): number
```

The one width a graph's cards share: the widest any of its rows' text needs (see `graphCardWidth`).

### `GraphCardText`

```ts
interface GraphCardText
```

What decides a graph card's width, besides its entity: the renderer's card text (see `GraphCanvasProps`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `comparing` | `"comparing"?: false \| true` | Whether the card shows a comparison, so its width also holds the status footer; one revision has none. |
| `detail` | `"detail"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): string \| undefined }` | A short code identifier right of the kind line, such as a version, cut to `cardTextMetrics.detailLength`. |
| `icon` | `"icon"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): string \| undefined }` | A card's icon before its kind line (`GraphCanvasProps.icon`), which the kind line makes room for. |
| `kindLine` | `"kindLine"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): KindLineText \| undefined }` | The renderer's kind line for an entity (`GraphCanvasProps.kindLine`); `entityKindLine` of its kind otherwise. |
| `prose` | `"prose"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): false \| true }` | Whether an entity's label is human language, measured in semibold sans; otherwise it is measured as code. |
| `status` | `"status"?: undefined \| { (row: EntityChange<Entity>): Array<StatusPart> \| undefined }` | In a comparison, the parts of a row's status footer (the domain's wording, else the comparison's own), which the card makes room for; leave it out for one revision, which has no status. |
| `textScale` | `"textScale"?: number` | The theme's extra-small type size over the default 12: text, and the cards that hold it, scale with it. |

### `graphCardWidth`

```ts
graphCardWidth(row: EntityChange<Entity>, text?: GraphCardText): number
```

The width a graph card's text needs: its widest line in either revision (the kind line with its icon, its note and
the detail at its right, the label, and in a comparison the status footer), between `cardWidthRange.min` and `.max`,
rounded up to a multiple of 4. A graph's cards share the widest of their widths (see `graphCardsWidth`), the same
at every progress, so no card resizes while scrubbing.

### `GraphFrame`

```ts
interface GraphFrame
```

What a graph transition draws at one progress (see `GraphTransition`), in layout units.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `edges` | `"edges": Array<TransitionEdge>` | Relationships visible at this progress; a rewired one may appear twice, its old and new routes crossfading. |
| `height` | `"height": number` | The drawing's height, interpolated between the layouts the frame moves between. |
| `junctions` | `"junctions": Array<Point>` | Join/split points of shared-prerequisite stages, when the frame is settled on a layout that has them. |
| `nodes` | `"nodes": Array<TransitionNode>` | Cards and boundaries visible at this progress, in the model's entity order. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The drawing's width, interpolated between the layouts the frame moves between. |

### `GraphLayout`

```ts
interface GraphLayout
```

A laid-out graph from `layoutGraph`, in layout units (CSS px at a zoom of 1). Shared: never change it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alignment` | `"alignment": "BALANCED" \| "LEFTDOWN" \| "LEFTUP" \| "RIGHTDOWN" \| "RIGHTUP"` | How this layout placed its cards (see `GraphLayoutOptions.alignment`). |
| `groups` | `"groups": Map<string, Array<string>>` | Compound module boundaries and their direct members. |
| `height` | `"height": number` | The height of the drawing, everything in it, its padding included. |
| `junctions` | `"junctions": Array<Point>` | Join/split points of shared-prerequisite stages (see `GraphLayoutOptions.junctions`). |
| `layerGap` | `"layerGap": number` | The space between layers this layout used (see `GraphLayoutOptions.layerGap`). |
| `points` | `"points": Map<string, Point>` | Card and boundary centres. |
| `ports` | `"ports": Map<string, RoutePorts>` | Where each route leaves and enters its cards, and where its S bends (see `RoutePorts`). |
| `routes` | `"routes": Map<string, Array<Point>>` | Relationship routes by layout edge ID (see `Spline`), in the cards' coordinates. |
| `shared` | `"shared": Set<string>` | Edges routed through a junction. |
| `sizes` | `"sizes": Map<string, { "height": number; "width": number }>` | Card and boundary sizes, keyed like `points`; a boundary is as large as it needs to enclose its members. |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The width of the drawing, everything in it, its padding included. |

### `GraphLayoutOptions`

```ts
interface GraphLayoutOptions
```

How `layoutGraph` lays out a graph; every option has a default.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `alignment` | `"alignment"?: "BALANCED" \| "LEFTDOWN" \| "LEFTUP" \| "RIGHTDOWN" \| "RIGHTUP"` | How to place the cards (see `GraphLayout.alignment`); chosen when absent. A transition passes its union's, so every step places its cards alike, in one ELK run. |
| `boundaries` | `"boundaries"?: ReadonlySet<string>` | Compound boundaries that stay boundaries even when nothing is left in them (see `moduleGroups`): a transition passes its union's, so no boundary turns into a card between steps. |
| `compound` | `"compound"?: Array<string> \| false \| true` | Group unambiguous containment-only entities into compound boundaries: `true` for `module`s (architecture), or the entity kinds that may become boundaries (infrastructure: modules, resource groups, parent resources). |
| `hints` | `"hints"?: ReadonlyMap<string, Point>` | Where cards were in a reference layout. ELK then keeps that order within each layer (semi-interactive crossing minimization) and still minimizes the crossings of long edges. Transitions pass their union layout, so cards keep their relative places from step to step. |
| `junctions` | `"junctions"?: false \| true` | Route each complete shared-prerequisite stage (two or more sources that each precede exactly the same two or more targets) through one join/split point (DAGs). |
| `layerGap` | `"layerGap"?: number` | Space between layers. Defaults to `layerGap`, grown (once) to fit the widest bundle of parallel runs that share one gap at full radius; pass a layout's own `layerGap` to lay another out with the same spacing, as a transition does for every layout it moves between. |
| `orientation` | `"orientation"?: "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | The layers' direction: `vertical` (the default) runs top to bottom, `horizontal` left to right. |

### `GraphTransition`

```ts
interface GraphTransition
```

Staged graph transition driven by the comparison's steps. Each step moves
the layout once, between two ELK layouts that keep the model order of the
union of both revisions, so survivors keep their relative places; entities
enter and leave in their own step's fade window; relationships fade with
the endpoint that brings or takes them, a relationship rewired between
survivors crossfades while the layout moves, and routes morph by
interpolating their spline control points. The layouts are computed once,
up front; the transition itself is a pure function of progress.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `call` | `(progress: number): GraphFrame` |  |
| `diff` | `"diff": GraphFrame` | Diff mode's static frame: the union layout with every entity and relationship of both revisions at full presence, survivors in their After version, and a rewired relationship drawn twice, on its old route and its new one (`TransitionEdge.part`). An extraction's frame is its own layout. |
| `layouts` | `"layouts": Array<GraphLayout>` | Every layout a frame interpolates between, in step order (Before first, After last). Frames stay inside their combined bounds, so framing from them never changes while scrubbing. |

### `GraphTransitionOptions`

```ts
interface GraphTransitionOptions
```

How `createGraphTransition` lays out a comparison.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `compound` | `"compound"?: Array<string> \| false \| true` | Group unambiguous containment-only entities into compound boundaries (see `GraphLayoutOptions.compound`). |
| `diffOnly` | `"diffOnly"?: { "heights"?: ReadonlyMap<string, number> }` | Lay out only diff mode's union (`GraphTransition.diff`), with cards of the given `heights` (taller for their text, see `diffCardText`); every frame is the diff frame. Leaves the staged layouts out, so it costs one layout. |
| `footer` | `"footer"?: false \| true` | Whether cards reserve a status footer (`cardFooterHeight`): a comparison's do; one revision's have no status, so by default an extraction's don't. |
| `grow` | `"grow"?: ReadonlyMap<string, number>` | How much taller a row's card is than its kind's in every layout, for rows that draw more (badge rows, say). |
| `held` | `"held"?: "after" \| "before"` | Lay out only the revision a held pane shows (`RendererEnvironment.pane`): every frame is that revision, placed in the union's order as the full transition places it, at the cost of two layouts instead of three. Its `layouts` hold that revision's alone, so a pane frames what it draws. |
| `include` | `"include"?: ReadonlySet<string>` | Entity rows to present; relationships need both endpoints. Defaults to every row. |
| `junctions` | `"junctions"?: false \| true` | Join complete shared-prerequisite stages (DAGs); see `GraphLayoutOptions.junctions`. |
| `orientation` | `"orientation"?: "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | The layers' direction: `vertical` (the default) runs top to bottom, `horizontal` left to right. |
| `widths` | `"widths"?: ReadonlyMap<string, number>` | Each row's card width, sized to its text in either revision (see `graphCardWidth`), the same in every layout so a card never resizes while scrubbing; `cardWidth` for a row without one. |

### `greedyWrap`

```ts
greedyWrap(widths: Array<number>, gap: number, limit: number): Array<Array<number>>
```

Greedy left-to-right wrapping at `limit`: each line takes items while they fit. An item wider than `limit` gets a line of its own.

### `hasIcon`

```ts
hasIcon(row: { "after"?: Entity | undefined; "before"?: Entity | undefined }, icon?: undefined | { (entity: Entity): string | undefined }): false | true
```

Whether a row shows an icon in either revision, so its kind line keeps room for one at every progress.

### `humanizeKind`

```ts
humanizeKind(kind: string): SummaryNoun
```

The host's word for an extraction kind, when the renderer gives none: its words (`target-framework` → `target
framework`), with a simple English plural (`workspace` → `workspaces`, `policy` → `policies`). A kind already in the
plural keeps it and is made singular (`dependencies` → `dependency`, `imports` → `import`); a kind ending in a
preposition reads the same in both (`applies to`), and so does an adjective (`24 hidden`, `5 not patchable`, `3
deprecated`; see `adjectivalKind`); `depends-on` is a dependency. Common prefixes stay hyphenated (`pre-release` →
`pre-releases`).

### `IconName`

```ts
type IconName = "added" | "additive" | "agent" | "application" | "blocked" | "breaking" | "bytecode" | "changed" | "collapse" | "comparator" | "compatible" | "credential" | "downgraded" | "enforced" | "error" | "exclude" | "expand" | "extractor" | "file" | "generated" | "hidden" | "host" | "import" | "include" | "info" | "modified" | "module" | "moved" | "namespace" | "network" | "other" | "policy" | "process" | "read" | "redeploy" | "removed" | "renamed" | "renderer" | "replace" | "rescoped" | "settings" | "unenforced" | "unknown" | "upgraded" | "varied" | "visible" | "warning" | "workload"
```

A name in the icon vocabulary (`iconNames`); validate untrusted input with `isIconName`.

### `identifierParts`

```ts
identifierParts(text: string): Array<LabelPart>
```

Splits a label into prose and the code identifiers inside it, so only the
identifiers draw in the monospace font: `GET /api/cart`, `app.js` and the
`Inter.woff2` of `Inter.woff2 (preloaded)` are code; `Install dependencies` is prose.

### `inflections`

```ts
inflections(route: Array<Point>, threshold?: number): number
```

How many times a route visibly changes the way it turns: the route is
followed as a polyline of fine samples, consecutive turns of one sign are
summed into runs, runs turning less than `threshold` degrees in all (the
imperceptible bends of a nearly straight stretch) are ignored, and the
count is how often the remaining runs change sign. One clean S has one.

### `interpolateSpline`

```ts
interpolateSpline(before: Array<Point>, after: Array<Point>, progress: number): Array<Point>
```

Morphs one route into another by interpolating control points, after
splitting both into segments that correspond by position along the route
(see `align`).

### `inwardNormal`

```ts
inwardNormal(point: Point, box: FaceBox): Point
```

The inward normal of the face of `box` that `point` lies on (the nearest
face): down into a top face, right into a left face, and so on.

### `isCardIconName`

```ts
isCardIconName(value: unknown): value is "activity" | "app-window" | "binary" | "blocks" | "book-open" | "bot" | "box" | "boxes" | "braces" | "brain" | "cable" | "chart-bar" | "cloud" | "code" | "code-xml" | "component" | "container" | "cpu" | "database" | "file" | "file-code" | "file-text" | "flask-conical" | "folder" | "folder-tree" | "gauge" | "git-branch" | "git-compare" | "git-merge" | "git-pull-request" | "globe" | "hammer" | "hard-drive" | "key-round" | "layers" | "layout-dashboard" | "library" | "list-tree" | "lock" | "mail" | "message-square" | "monitor" | "network" | "package" | "palette" | "panel-right" | "pickaxe" | "play" | "plug" | "puzzle" | "rocket" | "route" | "scan" | "scan-search" | "search" | "server" | "settings" | "shapes" | "shield" | "smartphone" | "sparkles" | "square-terminal" | "table" | "terminal" | "test-tube" | "user" | "users" | "webhook" | "workflow" | "wrench" | "zap"
```

Whether a value names a card icon (`cardIconNames`).

### `isChanged`

```ts
isChanged(change: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }): false | true
```

Whether a row carries a change worth emphasizing.

### `isFold`

```ts
isFold(id: string): false | true
```

Whether an item is a fold of left-out parts (`scopedModel` with `parts: 'fold'`), which opens with `ScopeView.expand`.

### `isKind`

```ts
isKind(change: EntityChange<Entity>, ...kinds: Array<string>): false | true
```

Whether either version of the row has one of `kinds`, so a row that changed kind matches both.

### `isSortable`

```ts
isSortable<T>(column: SortableColumn<T>): false | true
```

Whether a column can be sorted: it has a comparison, or a value to compare, and isn't marked unsortable.

### `joinSplines`

```ts
joinSplines(first: Array<Point>, second: Array<Point>): Array<Point>
```

Joins two chains end to start, bridging any gap with a straight cubic.
