### `kindLineLength`

```ts
kindLineLength: 25
```

Most characters of a kind line a boundary's heading shows; longer ones keep their end, the most specific part.

### `KindLineText`

```ts
interface KindLineText
```

A card's kind line, the small text above its label (see `GraphCanvasProps.kindLine` and `entityKindLine`).

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `identifier` | `"identifier"?: false \| true` | Draw `text` in monospace, as code (a resource type, a qualified name); sans when unset. |
| `note` | `"note"?: string` | Text after the kind line in sans, after a ` · ` (`aws_db_instance · Replace`); `Inferred` follows it when the entity is inferred. |
| `text` | `"text": string` | The text as drawn; a long one keeps its end, the most specific part (see `kindText`). |

### `kindNote`

```ts
kindNote(kind: KindLineText | undefined, inferred: false | true): string
```

The note after a kind line (the renderer's, then `Inferred`), or nothing.

### `kindText`

```ts
kindText(text: string, room?: number): string
```

A kind line cut to `room` characters, keeping its end: path-like kinds lose whole leading segments first.

### `LabelPart`

```ts
interface LabelPart
```

A run of a label: prose, or a code identifier inside it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | `"code": false \| true` | Whether the run is a code identifier, drawn in the monospace font. |
| `text` | `"text": string` | The run's text, verbatim, whitespace included; adjacent runs of the same kind are merged. |

### `languageCategory`

```ts
languageCategory(name: string): Category
```

The category of a language named by another tool (code statistics' tokei names), keeping that tool's label.

### `largestTurn`

```ts
largestTurn(route: Array<Point>): number
```

The largest turn a route makes one way without turning back, in degrees: 90
for an S of quarter circles, 180 for a hairpin or a cusp. A route between
facing sides never needs more than 90.

### `layerGap`

```ts
layerGap: number
```

Space between layers: room for a route's tail stub, two full turns (`routeRadius`) and its arrowhead's lead-in.

### `LayoutEdge`

```ts
interface LayoutEdge
```

A relationship to lay out (see `layoutGraph`). One with an endpoint missing from the nodes is left out.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `"from": string` | The source node's ID. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | Unique among the edges: the key of its route in `GraphLayout.routes`. |
| `kind` | `"kind": string` | The relationship's kind: a `contains` edge from a compound boundary draws as the boundary, with no route. |
| `to` | `"to": string` | The target node's ID. |

### `layoutFilter`

```ts
layoutFilter(previous: FilterPayload | undefined, message: FilterPayload): FilterPayload
```

What a host's `filter` lays out: whether it shows the Changes scope, and that scope's IDs (`scope`, or a host before
it's `ids`), as both `scope` and `ids`. `previous` while those are the same, so a summary figure or find, which only
recede what they leave out, lays nothing out again.

### `layoutGraph`

```ts
layoutGraph(nodes: Array<LayoutNode>, edges: Array<LayoutEdge>, options?: GraphLayoutOptions): Promise<GraphLayout>
```

Lays out a graph with ELK's layered algorithm: cards in layers (top to
bottom, or left to right for `horizontal`), relationships as splines that
leave and enter the cards' faces across the layers, containment-only
modules as compound boundaries. Browsers run ELK in a Worker. Layouts are
shared, never mutated: callers must not change the result.

### `LayoutNode`

```ts
interface LayoutNode
```

A graph node to lay out: a card of its kind's height (see `cardHeight`) and `cardWidth`, unless it gives its own.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `height` | `"height"?: number \| undefined` | The card's height, when its text makes it taller than its kind's (see `diffCardText`). |
| `id` | `"id": string` | Unique among the nodes: the key of its place in `GraphLayout.points` and `sizes`. |
| `kind` | `"kind": string` | The entity's kind, which sets the card's height (`cardHeight`) and whether it may become a boundary. |
| `width` | `"width"?: number \| undefined` | The card's width, when it is sized to its text (see `graphCardWidth`). |

### `leafChanges`

```ts
leafChanges(a: unknown, b: unknown, path: string): Array<{ "after": unknown; "before": unknown; "key": string }>
```

What differs between two values, down to the leaves: objects by key
(`hardwareProfile.vmSize`) and arrays of the same length by index
(`ingress[0].from_port`), in key order; anything else, or arrays whose
length changed, whole.

### `LegendShape`

```ts
type LegendShape = "circle" | "dashed" | "dotted" | "line" | "square"
```

One of `legendShapes`: a filled `square` or `circle`, or a solid, `dashed` or `dotted` stroke for relationships.

### `lineSpline`

```ts
lineSpline(from: Point, to: Point): Array<Point>
```

A straight segment as one cubic, so every route is a uniform chain.

### `maxZoom`

```ts
maxZoom(fit: number): number
```

The largest zoom multiple for a stage fitted at `fit`.

### `mixedChange`

```ts
mixedChange(change: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }): false | true
```

Whether a row changed in two ways, renamed and changed: no one hue is right for it, so a card draws it neutral and
each status word in its own hue (`pk-mixed-change`), never one change color inside another.

### `ModelStep`

```ts
type ModelStep = PresentedStep
```

One comparison step in presented-row space (see the SDK's `PresentedStep`).

### `moduleGroups`

```ts
moduleGroups(nodes: Array<LayoutNode>, edges: Array<LayoutEdge>, kinds?: Array<string>, keep?: ReadonlySet<string>): Map<string, Array<string>>
```

Only unambiguous containment-only entities of the boundary kinds (default `module`) become compound nodes. `keep`
names boundaries that stay boundaries with nothing left in them (a transition keeps its union's, so a module
emptied by removals stays a boundary rather than turning into a card).

### `motionWindow`

```ts
motionWindow(step: Pick<ScheduledStep, "radius" | "time"> & Partial<Pick<ScheduledStep, "lead" | "tail" | "travel">>): { "radius": number; "time": number }
```

The part of a step's window in which things move: all of it, less its
reading lead and tail.

### `moveEasing`

```ts
moveEasing(_easing: "add" | "remove" | "restructure", fraction: number): number
```

Layout easing for a step's move window: a pronounced ease-in-out (quintic
smootherstep) for every kind of step, so a move starts and ends softly and
a reversed comparison mirrors it exactly. Relationships morph on this same
clock as their cards.

### `nextSort`

```ts
nextSort<T>(sort: null | { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" | "descending" }, column: SortableColumn<T>): { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" | "descending" }
```

The sort a heading's activation asks for: the other direction for the sorted column, else its first direction.

### `nodeSpacing`

```ts
nodeSpacing: 24
```

Space ELK keeps between cards in a layer (ELK `spacing.nodeNode`), and between a card with no relationships and what
it is placed beside (see `placeUnlinked`). ELK's placement at this spacing decides each card's layer, order and
column; a graph on a grid then spreads its columns to `columnGap` (see `snapToGrid`), which leaves those decisions
as they are.

### `NoRouteError`

```ts
class NoRouteError extends Error
```

`boxEdge` found no route around the cards; `blocked` says which least-overlapping route there is.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `blocked` | `readonly "blocked": BlockedBoxEdge` |  |
| `captureStackTrace` | `static "captureStackTrace"(targetObject: object, constructorOpt?: Function \| undefined): void` |  |
| `cause` | `"cause"?: unknown` |  |
| `constructor` | `new (blocked: BlockedBoxEdge): NoRouteError` |  |
| `message` | `"message": string` |  |
| `name` | `"name": string` | `NoRouteError`. |
| `prepareStackTrace` | `static "prepareStackTrace"(err: Error, stackTraces: Array<CallSite>): any` |  |
| `stack` | `"stack"?: string` |  |
| `stackTraceLimit` | `static "stackTraceLimit": number` |  |

### `numericValue`

```ts
numericValue(change: EntityChange<Entity>, key: string, progress: number): number
```

A numeric `data` field interpolated between versions; a missing side counts as 0.

### `openingFloorPx`

```ts
openingFloorPx: 8
```

The smallest text, in CSS px, a zoomable canvas (a scroll container marked
`data-zoom`) opens with. It opens fitted, everything in view, unless that
draws its smallest text below this: then it opens zoomed until that text is
this size, at the content's start (its top left, or the top centre of a
centred layout), and the person scrolls and pans the rest; a diff, or a host's
focus (`RendererFocus`), opens on its changes instead. Fit to view still
shows everything, however small. The kit's `useStageZoom` applies it and the
built-in `opens-fitted` check verifies it. Added on 2026-11-10, the day
always fitting was adopted, after fitting drew the largest graphs' text at
2-6 px.

### `openingZoom`

```ts
openingZoom(fit: number, floor: number): number
```

The zoom multiple a stage fitted at `fit` opens at, given the scale `floor` at which its smallest text reaches
`openingFloorPx` (see `useOpeningFloor`; 0 when unknown): 1 (fitted) when the fit draws text at least that large,
else the multiple that brings it there.

```ts
otherToken: "color-border-emphasis"
```

The neutral color of categories past the palette.

### `paletteLegend`

```ts
paletteLegend(palette: Palette, title: string, limit?: number, shape?: "circle" | "dashed" | "dotted" | "line" | "square" | undefined): RendererLegend
```

The host legend for a palette: the heaviest categories with their swatches,
then the rest (categories sharing the neutral color, or past `limit`) as one
"N other types" item.

### `PaletteOptions`

```ts
interface PaletteOptions
```

How `categoryPalette` assigns colors beyond its defaults.

| Member | Signature | Description |

### `parseStageCover`

```ts
parseStageCover(token: string | undefined): Array<CoverRect> | undefined
```

The host's `stage-cover` theme token as rectangles: `x y width height` in CSS px, separated by commas. Undefined when
the host sends none (the renderer keeps to `stage-inset-top`, if any); empty when it sends one that covers nothing.

### `parseTableSort`

```ts
parseTableSort(value: false | number | string | true | undefined): null | { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" | "descending" }
```

The sort a sort control's value names; `null` for `none` or anything else.

### `partOwners`

```ts
partOwners(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction> | undefined): ReadonlyMap<string, string>
```

The change each further part of a split or merge presents, by its row's ID: the host's filter names the change, and
the part is kept with it (`InteractionOptions.partOf`).

### `pillMetrics`

```ts
pillMetrics: { "baseline": 13; "height": 17; "padding": 3 }
```

A pill around one line of card text at the type scale's default size (12), aligned optically rather than by its box:
the space above a capital E's top, below its baseline, left of its stem and right of a last capital H's right stem is
about the same (to within a card unit: the pill is a whole number of them wide), with every edge on a whole card unit. The text's baseline is `baseline` under the
pill's top: the sans fonts' cap height is about 8.6 card units, which leaves about 4.4 above it and 4 below. Its
`padding` beyond the text's advance on each side is 3, which the glyphs' own side bearings (about 1 card unit) make
about 4 to their stems. Measured from rendered pixels with the renderer testing package's `opticalInsets`. See
`textPill`.

### `placeBadges`

```ts
placeBadges(values: Array<string | { "prose"?: true; "text": string; "tone"?: "highlight" | "quiet" }>, room: number, textScale?: number): Array<{ "prose": false | true; "row": number; "text": string; "tone": "highlight" | "quiet" | undefined; "width": number; "x": number }>
```

Badges in rows `room` wide, each as wide as its text; one too wide for a row ends in an ellipsis. Quiet tags start a
row of their own after the pills.

### `placedAttribute`

```ts
placedAttribute: "data-projections-placed"
```

Marks a scroll container whose renderer places its own opening view (see `useScrollAnchor`): the shell leaves it.

```ts
plainCategory(key: string, label?: string): Category
```

A category without a language, such as an entity kind.

### `plainProse`

```ts
plainProse(text: string): string
```

Prose as plain text, without code markers: for titles, labels and assistive text.

### `pluralKind`

```ts
pluralKind(kind: string): string
```

A kind's plural, as English forms it: `services`, `classes`, `dependencies`. Kinds are shown verbatim otherwise.

### `Point`

```ts
interface Point
```

A point or a vector in drawing units, with y growing downward.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `x` | `"x": number` | Distance rightward. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | Distance downward. |

### `polylineCrossings`

```ts
polylineCrossings(pa: Array<Point>, pb: Array<Point>, ignore?: Array<Point>, radius?: number): Array<Point>
```

Where two sampled routes (see `sampleSpline`) cross, as `routeCrossings`.

### `polylinesCross`

```ts
polylinesCross(pa: Array<Point>, pb: Array<Point>, ignore?: Array<Point>, radius?: number): false | true
```

Whether two sampled routes cross anywhere (see `polylineCrossings`), stopping at the first crossing.

### `portInset`

```ts
portInset: 16
```

Least distance from a port to the corners of its side.

### `portSpacing`

```ts
portSpacing: 16
```

Most space between the ports of neighbouring routes on one side of a card.

### `presentedEmphasis`

```ts
presentedEmphasis(change: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }, highlighting: number): number
```

How strongly to emphasize a change, ignoring steps: the host's
`highlighting` for changed rows, 0 for everything else. Highlighting is
exactly 0 at both endpoints, so nothing looks changed there. Renderers use
the step-scoped `RendererProps.emphasis` (see `stepEmphasis`) instead.

### `proseLines`

```ts
proseLines(text: string, room: number, textScale?: number, max?: number): Array<string>
```

Human text in sans on lines `room` card units wide: whole words fill each line (a word wider than a line is cut), and
text needing more than `max` lines ends its last in an ellipsis. Empty text is no lines.

### `ProseSpan`

```ts
interface ProseSpan
```

A run of prose text: human language, or inline code.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `code` | `"code": false \| true` |  |
| `text` | `"text": string` |  |

### `proseSpans`

```ts
proseSpans(text: string): Array<ProseSpan>
```

Splits prose into its human-language and inline-code runs, unescaping both.

### `RadiusStep`

```ts
type RadiusStep = "full" | "lg" | "md" | "sm"
```

Steps of the corner radius scale: `sm` (6px) to `lg` (10px), and `full` for pills; `md` is the `radius` token.

### `ramp`

```ts
ramp(progress: number, center: number, radius: number): number
```

0 before `center - radius`, 1 after `center + radius`, smooth in between.

### `readBorderWidths`

```ts
readBorderWidths(element: Element | null): BorderWidths
```

The border widths in effect on `element`, falling back to the defaults where unset.

### `readingShare`

```ts
readingShare: 1
```

The reading policy: how long, in step slots, a step that takes something
away keeps still to show it before it leaves. The step's emphasis rises over
the first fifth of its reading part and holds while nothing moves, so what
is about to disappear is readable (about a second at 1× speed with the host's
default pace, `timelineSlots`) before it fades and its gap closes. The other
changes need no reading part: an arrival fades in already emphasized and
stays so through the hold after its step until the host's endpoint fade, and
a change that stays is emphasized as it changes. This is the one place
reading time is decided; renderers never add their own.

### `RendererLegend`

```ts
interface RendererLegend
```

A renderer's legend: an optional title and its items; no items clears it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | `"items": Array<LegendItem>` | The entries in display order, at most `rendererLimits.legendItems`. |
| `title` | `"title"?: string` | A heading for the legend, 1 to `rendererLimits.legendLabel` characters. |

### `rendererSummary`

```ts
rendererSummary(init: RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" | "diff" | "side-by-side" | "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } | RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" }, nouns?: undefined | { (kind: string, collection: "entities" | "relationships"): SummaryNoun | false | undefined } | { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun | false }, facts?: Array<SummaryFactItem>): RendererSummary
```

The summary a kit renderer posts for a document: a figure per extraction kind with its counts, worded with the
renderer's `nouns` (see `SummaryNouns`) and the host's words for the rest, then the renderer's domain `facts`
(see `SummaryFacts`), together at most `rendererLimits.summaryItems`. The shell posts it whenever the document, the
nouns or the facts change, so a renderer only names its kinds and states its facts.

### `RendererSummary`

```ts
interface RendererSummary
```

A renderer's summary: its figures in display order; no items returns the bar to the host's own words.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | `"items": Array<SummaryCountItem \| SummaryFactItem>` | The figures, at most `rendererLimits.summaryItems`, in the order the bar shows them. |

### `roundedSpline`

```ts
roundedSpline(polyline: Array<Point>, radius?: number): Array<Point>
```

An orthogonal route as one smooth chain of cubics: collinear and repeated
points are dropped, and every corner becomes a quarter curve whose radius is
at most half of each adjacent leg, so a dogleg between layers reads as one
S-curve, the same as a spline route, and a short jog as a gentle wave rather
than a stair-step.

### `routeBoxEdge`

```ts
routeBoxEdge(from: ArrowBox, target: ArrowBox, obstacles?: Array<ArrowBox>, style?: "curved" | "orthogonal", ports?: { "end"?: Point; "start"?: Point }, outset?: number, tracks?: Array<number>): BlockedBoxEdge | BoxEdge
```

`boxEdge`, with no route around the cards as a result rather than an error: a `BlockedBoxEdge` with the
least-overlapping route, for the caller to draw and report or to refuse. Boxes that can't be joined at all still
throw a `RangeError`.

### `routeCrossings`

```ts
routeCrossings(a: Array<Point>, b: Array<Point>, ignore?: Array<Point>, radius?: number): Array<Point>
```

Where two routes cross: their sampled courses intersect anywhere but
within `ignore` of the given shared points (a common source port, or the
common target card they converge on).

### `RouteOptions`

```ts
interface RouteOptions
```

How `sBend` and `sTurn` shape an S; every option has a default.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `band` | `"band"?: readonly [number, number]` | Where along the axis the S may turn, as distances from `start`: the stubs fill the rest. Defaults to everything after `routeTail` (when there is room for it) up to the lead-in. |
| `lead` | `"lead"?: false \| true` | End with the arrowhead's straight lead-in (`arrowHeadReach` long); default true. |
| `radius` | `"radius"?: number` | Largest turn radius; default `routeRadius`. |
| `track` | `"track"?: number` | Moves the S's middle (its crossing run) this far along the axis from the band's middle: a track in a shared gap. |

### `RoutePorts`

```ts
interface RoutePorts
```

Where a route leaves and enters its cards, relative to the card centres,
and, for a route that is one S, where along it the S bends: from `bend[0]`
after the source port to `bend[1]` before the end of the bend's span (the
start of the arrowhead's lead-in). Transitions redraw such routes as one S
between the moving cards with these values interpolated (`gappedBend`)
rather than morphing control points, so they stay one clean S in every frame.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `bend` | `"bend"?: readonly [number, number]` | A direct S's band: how far after the source and before the lead-in its turns are confined (see `gappedBend`). |
| `from` | `"from": Point` | Where the route leaves its source, relative to the source card's centre. |
| `to` | `"to": Point` | Where the route enters its target, relative to the target card's centre. |
| `track` | `"track"?: number` | The S's track in a gap it shares: how far its crossing run sits from the band's middle. |

### `routeRadius`

```ts
routeRadius: 20
```

The largest radius of a route's turns, in drawing units (CSS px at a zoom of 1): wide enough to read as one
drafted S, tight enough that layers stay close (see `layerGap`).

### `routesCross`

```ts
routesCross(a: Array<Point>, b: Array<Point>, ignore?: Array<Point>, radius?: number): false | true
```

Whether two routes cross (see `routeCrossings`).

### `routeTail`

```ts
routeTail: 8
```

Shortest straight stub leaving a source before a route turns.

### `routeTracks`

```ts
routeTracks(runs: Array<TrackRun>, spacing?: number): Array<number>
```

Tracks (`RouteOptions.track`) for S routes drawn together, so no two
crossing runs lie on one another: runs in one gap whose spans across the
axis overlap are spread `trackSpacing` apart about their common middle,
ordered so they cross as little as possible (of two routes heading the same
way, the one leaving later turns first, clear of the other's first leg).
Routes leaving one point the same way share their first stretch, as a
trunk. Returns 0 for a run that shares its place with none.

```ts
rowIcons(row: { "after"?: Entity | undefined; "before"?: Entity | undefined }, icon: undefined | { (entity: Entity): string | undefined }): ["activity" | "app-window" | "binary" | "blocks" | "book-open" | "bot" | "box" | "boxes" | "braces" | "brain" | "cable" | "chart-bar" | "cloud" | "code" | "code-xml" | "component" | "container" | "cpu" | "database" | "file" | "file-code" | "file-text" | "flask-conical" | "folder" | "folder-tree" | "gauge" | "git-branch" | "git-compare" | "git-merge" | "git-pull-request" | "globe" | "hammer" | "hard-drive" | "key-round" | "layers" | "layout-dashboard" | "library" | "list-tree" | "lock" | "mail" | "message-square" | "monitor" | "network" | "package" | "palette" | "panel-right" | "pickaxe" | "play" | "plug" | "puzzle" | "rocket" | "route" | "scan" | "scan-search" | "search" | "server" | "settings" | "shapes" | "shield" | "smartphone" | "sparkles" | "square-terminal" | "table" | "terminal" | "test-tube" | "user" | "users" | "webhook" | "workflow" | "wrench" | "zap" | undefined, "activity" | "app-window" | "binary" | "blocks" | "book-open" | "bot" | "box" | "boxes" | "braces" | "brain" | "cable" | "chart-bar" | "cloud" | "code" | "code-xml" | "component" | "container" | "cpu" | "database" | "file" | "file-code" | "file-text" | "flask-conical" | "folder" | "folder-tree" | "gauge" | "git-branch" | "git-compare" | "git-merge" | "git-pull-request" | "globe" | "hammer" | "hard-drive" | "key-round" | "layers" | "layout-dashboard" | "library" | "list-tree" | "lock" | "mail" | "message-square" | "monitor" | "network" | "package" | "palette" | "panel-right" | "pickaxe" | "play" | "plug" | "puzzle" | "rocket" | "route" | "scan" | "scan-search" | "search" | "server" | "settings" | "shapes" | "shield" | "smartphone" | "sparkles" | "square-terminal" | "table" | "terminal" | "test-tube" | "user" | "users" | "webhook" | "workflow" | "wrench" | "zap" | undefined]
```

A row's card icon in each revision, or undefined where it names none in `cardIconNames`.

### `sameValue`

```ts
sameValue(a: unknown, b: unknown): false | true
```

Structural equality of extracted JSON values; object key order never matters.

### `sampleSpline`

```ts
sampleSpline(points: Array<Point>, spacing?: number): Array<Point>
```

Points along a chain, about `spacing` apart, for geometry checks.

### `sBend`

```ts
sBend(start: Point, end: Point, axis: Point, options?: RouteOptions): Array<Point> | undefined
```

The S from `start` to `end`, leaving and arriving along `axis` (a unit
vector: down for a top-to-bottom graph, right for left to right). Undefined
when `end` is not far enough ahead of `start` along the axis for one.

### `ScheduledStep`

```ts
interface ScheduledStep extends PresentedStep
```

A step placed on the progress axis. The step changes only inside its window
`[time - radius, time + radius]`; windows never overlap, and consecutive
windows are separated by a hold of length `hold` in which nothing moves. A
step that takes something away in its direction of travel reads it first
(see `readingShare`): a still part of its window, its `lead` forward or its
`tail` for explicit reverse steps played backward, in which what is about
to leave is emphasized and read before it goes.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `adds` | `"adds"?: false \| true` | Whether the step adds an entity or relationship (absent: whether `kind` is `add`). |
| `declaredKind` | `"declaredKind"?: "add" \| "remove" \| "restructure"` | The kind the comparator declared, when it declared one. |
| `entities` | `"entities": Array<string>` | Presented entity row IDs that change in this step. |
| `hold` | `"hold": number` | Length of the still interval between this window and a neighbouring one. |
| `index` | `"index": number` | The step's position in its order, from 0; a final step for unplaced changes comes last. |
| `kind` | `"kind": "add" \| "remove" \| "restructure"` | The kind the step animates as, inferred from its entity rows. |
| `lead` | `"lead"?: number` | Length of the still part at the start of the step's window (lowest progress) in which what it removes is emphasized and read before it fades. 0 or absent for a step that removes nothing, and travelling backward. |
| `radius` | `"radius": number` | Half-width of the step's window, its reading lead and tail included. |
| `relationships` | `"relationships": Array<string>` | Presented relationship row IDs that change in this step. |
| `removes` | `"removes"?: false \| true` | Whether the step removes an entity or relationship (absent: whether `kind` is `remove`). |
| `summary` | `"summary"?: string` | The comparator's one-line description of the step, for captions; absent when it gave none. |
| `tail` | `"tail"?: number` | Length of the still part at the end of the step's window (highest progress): an explicit reverse step played backward reads what it takes away (the forward additions) there. 0 or absent otherwise. |
| `time` | `"time": number` | Centre of the step's window, in [0, 1]. |
| `travel` | `"travel": -1 \| 1` | The direction this schedule is travelled in: 1 forward (and for `mirror` order either way), -1 for `explicit` `reverseSteps` played backward. |

### `scheduleSteps`

```ts
scheduleSteps<S extends PresentedStep = PresentedStep>(order: { "reverse": "explicit" | "mirror"; "reverseSteps"?: Array<S> | undefined; "steps": Array<S> }, direction?: -1 | 1 | undefined): Array<S & { "hold": number; "lead": number; "radius": number; "tail": number; "time": number; "travel": -1 | 1 }>
```

The steps placed on the progress axis, in ascending time. Playing forward,
or with `mirror` reverse order, uses the forward steps; playing backward
with `explicit` reverse order places `reverseSteps` so that the first one
happens first when leaving progress 1. Both schedules agree at the
endpoints, where every step has either not started or finished. A step that
removes something gets a reading lead; travelling backward through explicit
reverse steps, one that adds something gets a reading tail, the part that
backward travel enters first. Use a `DirectionLatch` to choose `direction`.

### `scopedModel`

```ts
scopedModel<X extends Extraction>(model: ComparisonModel<X>, shown: ReadonlySet<string>, parts?: "fold" | "omit" | "whole", open?: ReadonlySet<string>): ScopedModel<X>
```

A model of only what a scope shows, for a canvas to lay out: the shown entities and their `parts` (left out, whole or
folded), and the relationships between them. A relationship is kept only when both its ends are: a changed one always
is (its ends are its context), an unchanged one between shown items stays, and none is ever drawn to an item the
scope leaves out. Steps keep their kept rows, and a step left with none is dropped. Every other item takes no room.
A fold is an unchanged entity of its parts' most common kind, labeled with their counts and contained by its entity
in each revision that has it. A fold in `open` shows its parts and stays, labeled `Hide …` with `data.open`, as the
way to fold them again.

### `ScopedModel`

```ts
interface ScopedModel<X extends Extraction = Extraction>
```

A model of only what a scope shows (`scopedModel`), and the parts each fold in it stands for.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `folds` | `"folds": ReadonlyMap<string, Array<string>>` | Each fold's left-out parts, by the fold's ID. |
| `model` | `"model": ComparisonModel<X>` | The model of what the scope shows, with the folds standing for left-out parts. |

### `ScopedParts`

```ts
type ScopedParts = "fold" | "omit" | "whole"
```

How `scopedModel` treats the parts of a shown entity (the items it contains): left out; kept whole, for a card that
draws its parts as one; or folded, each entity's left-out parts standing as one more part, a fold (`foldPrefix`).

### `ScopeView`

```ts
interface ScopeView extends ChangesScope
```

The Changes scope as a kit renderer receives it (`RendererProps.scope`): what it shows, every item's model, and a way
to show more of it.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `all` | `"all": ComparisonModel<Extraction>` | The model of every item: what a canvas's `model` (`MountOptions.scope` `subset`) narrows. |
| `changes` | `"changes": ReadonlySet<string>` | The change rows in scope, by row ID. |
| `collapse` | `"collapse"(ids: Iterable<string, any, any>): void` | Folds these open folds again, or stops showing items `expand` added. |
| `context` | `"context": ReadonlySet<string>` | The unchanged rows shown to read them: their relationships' endpoints and the items that contain them. |
| `expand` | `"expand"(ids: Iterable<string, any, any>): void` | Shows these items too, or opens these folds (`isFold`), until the host's scope changes. A canvas lays them out with the rest; an open fold stays, as the way to fold its parts again. |
| `shown` | `"shown": ReadonlySet<string>` | Both: every row the scope shows. |

### `scrolledPadding`

```ts
scrolledPadding(__0: { "height": number; "inset": { "bottom": number; "top": number }; "own": { "top": number; "y": number }; "view": number }): { "top": number; "y": number }
```

The top and bottom (`y`) padding of a drawing drawn larger than its fit, CSS px, so it clears bands of `inset.top`
and `inset.bottom` at the ends of a stage `view` px tall: `height` is the drawing's own height at the drawn scale.
While it still fits the stage's height it sits centred (`margin: auto`) and keeps `own` where that leaves it clear,
else just enough more at the end it reaches to clear the band; once that padding no longer fits, the drawing scrolls
and each end is padded at least its band, so its first and last rows can scroll clear.

### `ScrollStart`

```ts
type ScrollStart = { "x": number; "y": number } | { (view: { "height": number; "scale": number; "width": number }): { "left": number; "top": number } }
```

Where content that overflows its opening view starts: fractions of its scroll range (`{x: 0, y: 0}` is the top
left, `{x: 0.5, y: 0}` the top centre of a centred layout), or a function of the drawn scale (and the view's size,
for a start that centres something) that returns the scroll offsets, for content whose reading start isn't a corner
of its bounds (see `contentStart`). Offsets are clamped to the scroll range. A start depends only on the content,
the scale and the view, never on highlighting, so the same content always opens at the same place; while the view
opens, it is placed again whenever the view settles to another size. Content fitted to the view never overflows; a
start places content opened at the text floor (see `openingFloorPx`), opened on a focus, or a stage that can't be
fitted yet, such as one laid out before its pane has a height.

### `settle`

```ts
settle(value: number): number
```

Ease that settles without overshoot: fast departure, gentle arrival.

### `smootherstep`

```ts
smootherstep(value: number): number
```

Quintic smootherstep: a pronounced ease-in-out whose speed and acceleration
are both zero at either end, so a move starts and stops without a jolt.

### `smoothJoins`

```ts
smoothJoins(route: Array<Point>): Array<Point>
```

A route with every join made tangent-continuous: at each join between
segments, the two handles are turned onto one line (their lengths kept), so
interpolated routes never show a kink.

### `smoothRoute`

```ts
smoothRoute(polyline: Array<Point>, axis: Point, options?: RouteOptions): Array<Point> | undefined
```

An orthogonal route (legs along and across the axis, as ELK's router draws
them around cards) as a chain of clean S bends: every jog across the axis
becomes one S centred on it, using up to half of each neighbouring leg, so
the route keeps ELK's course and has one inflection per jog. Undefined when
the route doesn't alternate legs along and across the axis, moving forward
along it (a route that loops back).

### `smoothstep`

```ts
smoothstep(value: number): number
```

Cubic smoothstep of `value` clamped to [0, 1]: eases in and out, with zero speed at either end. `ramp` uses it.

### `SortableColumn`

```ts
interface SortableColumn<T>
```

What the table's ordering needs of a column.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `firstDirection` | `"firstDirection"?: "ascending" \| "descending"` | The direction a first click on the heading sorts in; `ascending` by default. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | Stable ID: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, at most 48 characters. It names the column in the sort control. |
| `label` | `"label": string` | The column's heading, in words. |
| `sort` | `"sort"?: "number" \| "string" \| false \| { (a: T, b: T): number }` | How the column orders rows (see `ColumnSort`). |
| `value` | `"value"?: { (item: T): false \| null \| number \| string \| true \| undefined }` | The cell's value in one version of a row: what the column sorts by, and shows unless the column renders its own. |

### `SortDirection`

```ts
type SortDirection = "ascending" | "descending"
```

Which way a column sorts.

### `sortedVersion`

```ts
sortedVersion<T>(row: TableRow<T>): T
```

The version of a row a table sorts and labels it by: After's, or Before's for a removed row.

### `SortTableOptions`

```ts
interface SortTableOptions<T>
```

Options of `sortTableRows`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `changesFirst` | `"changesFirst"?: false \| true \| undefined` | Changed rows first, each part in the sort's order. |
| `label` | `"label"?: undefined \| { (item: T): string }` | The row's label for breaking ties, before its ID: the first column's value by default. |
| `locale` | `"locale"?: string \| undefined` | BCP 47 locale for comparing strings; the runtime's by default. |

### `sortTableRows`

```ts
sortTableRows<T, R extends TableRow<T>>(rows: Array<R>, columns: Array<SortableColumn<T>>, sort: null | { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" | "descending" }, options?: SortTableOptions<T>): Array<R>
```

Rows in the table's order: by `sort`'s column (`null` keeps the given order), with rows missing a value last in
either direction, then by label and ID, so equal rows never swap. A comparison sorts each row by After's version, or
Before's for a removed row, so the order is the same at every point of the transition and rows never move while it
plays. `changesFirst` puts changed rows (added, removed, modified, renamed) before the rest.

### `SpaceStep`

```ts
type SpaceStep = 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8
```

Steps of the space scale: `space-1` (4px) to `space-8` (48px).

### `Spline`

```ts
type Spline = Array<Point>
```

A relationship's route: a chain of cubic Bézier segments, `[start, c1, c2,
p1, c1, c2, p2, …]`, so its length is `3n + 1` for `n` segments. Routes
start on the source card's face and end on the target card's face.

### `splinePath`

```ts
splinePath(points: Array<Point>): string
```

The SVG path data of a chain.

### `spreadPorts`

```ts
spreadPorts(count: number, length: number, spacing?: number, inset?: number): Array<number>
```

Where `count` routes meet one side of a card (or a row), as offsets from
the side's middle, in order: spread evenly over a band centred on the side,
`spacing` apart at most and never closer than `inset` to its ends. One
route meets the middle.

### `Stage`

```ts
interface Stage
```

The state after some number of steps: which entity rows are present, and
which rows (entities and relationships) already show their after version.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `active` | `"active": ReadonlySet<string>` | Entity row IDs present in this stage (and included, see `createStagedTimeline`). |
| `settled` | `"settled": ReadonlySet<string>` | Row IDs, entities and relationships, whose step has passed, so they show their After version. |

### `StagedTimeline`

```ts
interface StagedTimeline
```

A comparison's steps as stages and windows, from `createStagedTimeline`; every function is pure in `progress`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `at` | `"at"(progress: number): { "from": number; "mix": number; "to": number }` | The two stages a frame interpolates between, and how far. |
| `local` | `"local"(id: string, progress: number): number` | Progress through a row's own step, 0 before it starts and 1 after it ends; always 0 for a row no step changes. |
| `presence` | `"presence"(id: string, progress: number): number` | Opacity of an entity row: entering and leaving rows fade in their step's window. |
| `relationships` | `"relationships"(stage: Stage): Array<{ "from": string; "row": EntityChange<Relationship>; "to": string }>` | Relationships present in a stage, resolved to entity row endpoints. |
| `rowPresence` | `"rowPresence"(id: string, progress: number): { "opacity": number; "size": number }` | Presence of an entity row in a list: `size` is the share of its slot it occupies, `opacity` its visibility. A removal fades, then its slot closes during the step's move window; an addition's slot opens, then it fades in. Both are 1 for survivors and 0 for rows absent at this point. |
| `stages` | `"stages": Array<Stage>` | `stages[0]` is the before state; `stages[k + 1]` follows step `k`. |
| `version` | `"version"<T>(row: EntityChange<T>, stage: Stage): T` | The version of a row a stage shows. |
| `windows` | `"windows": Array<StepWindows>` | Each scheduled step's windows (see `stepWindows`), in order: `windows[k]` moves `stages[k]` to `stages[k + 1]`. |

### `StageZoom`

```ts
interface StageZoom
```

The zoom `useStageZoom` applies: draw the content at `scale`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `keep` | `"keep": { (): void }` | Keeps the view where the caller just scrolled it, as though the person had: later changes of scale keep its middle. |
| `scale` | `"scale": number` | The drawn scale: the fitted scale times the zoom; 0 until the stage has been measured. |
| `zoom` | `"zoom": number` | The zoom multiple of the fitted scale (1 is fitted); a scroll container carries it as `data-zoom`. |

### `StageZoomOptions`

```ts
interface StageZoomOptions
```

Where `useStageZoom` opens the view; by default fitted, or at the text floor when fitting draws text too small.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `floor` | `"floor"?: number` | The scale at which the smallest text reaches `openingFloorPx` (see `useOpeningFloor`): content whose fit is smaller opens at it instead and scrolls. Measure it over everything the stage frames (both endpoints of a transition), so it never changes while scrubbing. |
| `hold` | `"hold"?: { "key": unknown; "scale": number }` | A drawn scale (CSS px per content unit) to keep: whenever `key` changes, the zoom becomes the multiple of the fit that draws at `scale` (within the zoom range), as though the person had zoomed there, so a view that changes its content's size, and with it the fit, keeps its zoom. |
| `opening` | `"opening"?: { "centred"?: false \| true; "start": { "x": number; "y": number } \| { (view: { "height": number; "scale": number; "width": number }): { "left": number; "top": number } }; "zoom": number }` | An opening view chosen by the caller instead, for example on a focus (see `RendererFocus`): its zoom multiple of the fit (clamped to the zoom range) and where it starts. Like the default, it holds until the person zooms or pans. `centred`: the start centres a focus in the view, so it isn't moved clear of a stage cover as a reading start is. |
| `start` | `"start"?: { "x": number; "y": number } \| { (view: { "height": number; "scale": number; "width": number }): { "left": number; "top": number } }` | Where content that overflows the opening view starts (default the top left; see `ScrollStart`). |

### `statusGlyphs`

```ts
statusGlyphs: Record<"added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed" | "unchanged", string>
```

Text glyphs for each change (`+` added, `−` removed, `~` modified, `→`
renamed), for plain-text contexts such as titles and the host's text view.
Rendered status draws `statusIcons` instead, always beside the word.

### `statusIcons`

```ts
statusIcons: Record<"added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed", "added" | "additive" | "agent" | "application" | "blocked" | "breaking" | "bytecode" | "changed" | "collapse" | "comparator" | "compatible" | "credential" | "downgraded" | "enforced" | "error" | "exclude" | "expand" | "extractor" | "file" | "generated" | "hidden" | "host" | "import" | "include" | "info" | "modified" | "module" | "moved" | "namespace" | "network" | "other" | "policy" | "process" | "read" | "redeploy" | "removed" | "renamed" | "renderer" | "replace" | "rescoped" | "settings" | "unenforced" | "unknown" | "upgraded" | "varied" | "visible" | "warning" | "workload">
```

The icon that accompanies each change's word (see `Icon`).

### `statusLabels`

```ts
statusLabels: Record<"added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed" | "unchanged", string>
```

The word for each change, in sentence case, as status text and accessible names say it (`Added`, `Renamed`).

### `StatusPart`

```ts
interface StatusPart
```

One icon-and-word part of a change's status. `status` chooses the change
color; a renderer may word a domain's changes its own way (`−/+ Replace`)
as long as glyph and word say what the color says.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `glyph` | `"glyph": string` | The part as a text glyph, for plain-text contexts (titles, keys); rendered status shows `icon`. |
| `icon` | `"icon": "added" \| "additive" \| "agent" \| "application" \| "blocked" \| "breaking" \| "bytecode" \| "changed" \| "collapse" \| "comparator" \| "compatible" \| "credential" \| "downgraded" \| "enforced" \| "error" \| "exclude" \| "expand" \| "extractor" \| "file" \| "generated" \| "hidden" \| "host" \| "import" \| "include" \| "info" \| "modified" \| "module" \| "moved" \| "namespace" \| "network" \| "other" \| "policy" \| "process" \| "read" \| "redeploy" \| "removed" \| "renamed" \| "renderer" \| "replace" \| "rescoped" \| "settings" \| "unenforced" \| "unknown" \| "upgraded" \| "varied" \| "visible" \| "warning" \| "workload"` | The icon drawn beside the word (see `Icon`). |
| `label` | `"label": string` | The word, in sentence case (`Added`, or a domain's own such as `Replace`). |
| `status` | `"status": "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "renamed" \| "unchanged"` | The change this part stands for, which chooses its color. |

### `statusParts`

```ts
statusParts(change: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }): Array<StatusPart>
```

A change's status as glyph-and-word parts: one, or two for a renamed and otherwise changed item.

### `stepEmphasis`

```ts
stepEmphasis(schedule: Array<ScheduledStep>, progress: number, highlighting: number, pane?: "after" | "before" | undefined): EmphasisOf
```

Change emphasis scoped to each change's own comparison step: a change shows
none of the host's highlighting until its step's window begins (in the
direction the schedule is travelled, so an explicit reverse order mirrors
it), rises over the start of the window, then follows the host's
highlighting, which is exactly 0 at both endpoints. Earlier steps never
pre-tint later changes. Rows no step places use the host's highlighting.
A held pane of side by side or swipe (`pane`) is a static comparison, not a
moment of the transition: every change it shows follows the host's
highlighting alike, so Before marks its removals as After marks its
additions.

### `stepEnds`

```ts
stepEnds(schedule: Array<Pick<ScheduledStep, "hold" | "radius" | "time">>, direction?: -1 | 1 | undefined): Array<number>
```

Progress values where a host may hold between steps: for each step, the
middle of the hold that follows it in the direction of travel (forward,
after its window; backward, before it), so seeking there always shows a
settled frame. Endpoints are omitted because hosts always stop there.
Report them with `client.steps`.

### `stepHolds`

```ts
stepHolds(schedule: Array<Pick<ScheduledStep, "radius" | "time">>): Array<{ "end": number; "start": number }>
```

The still intervals of a schedule, in ascending order: before the first
window, between consecutive windows and after the last. Nothing driven by
the schedule moves inside them.

### `stepHoldShare`

```ts
stepHoldShare: number
```

The hold policy: the share of every step's slot in which nothing moves. Host
playback is continuous, so a still interval between consecutive windows is
what makes shapes visibly settle at each step while progress keeps moving.
The headroom before the first and after the last step is at least as long.
This is the one place step holds are decided; renderers never add their own.

### `StepKind`

```ts
type StepKind = "add" | "remove" | "restructure"
```

What a step does, which decides its choreography (`stepWindows` in the kit): `remove` fades items out, then closes
the gap; `add` makes room, then fades items in; `restructure` moves and rewires what stays.

### `stepProgress`

```ts
stepProgress(step: Pick<ScheduledStep, "radius" | "time"> & Partial<Pick<ScheduledStep, "lead" | "tail" | "travel">>, progress: number): number
```

Progress through a step's motion (`motionWindow`): 0 until it starts moving,
after any reading lead, and 1 once it stops, before any reading tail, so it
is constant in every hold and while reading. Measured from the centre, so
the middle of the motion is exactly one half. Ease it for motion.

### `stepWindows`

```ts
stepWindows(step: ScheduledStep, rows: ReadonlyMap<string, EntityChange<Entity>>): StepWindows
```

Sub-windows of one step's motion (`motionWindow`, after any reading lead in
which removals stay fully present while their emphasis is read). Removals
fade out over the first 35% of the motion, then the layout closes their gap
over the remaining 65%; additions are given room over the first 65%, then
fade in over the rest; a restructure moves for its whole window, crossfading
rewired relationships around its centre. A step that both removes and adds
entities (only custom comparators produce one) fades out for 20%, moves for
60% and fades in for 20%. Motion spans most of each step, and nothing fades
while the cards around it move.

### `StepWindows`

```ts
interface StepWindows
```

How one scheduled step uses its window.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `easing` | `"easing": "add" \| "remove" \| "restructure"` | What the step does: `remove` fades out then closes gaps, `add` makes room then fades in, `restructure` moves and crossfades around its centre (as does a step that both removes and adds). |
| `fadeIn` | `"fadeIn": Window` | Where arriving entities fade in. |
| `fadeOut` | `"fadeOut": Window` | Where leaving entities fade out. |
| `move` | `"move": Window` | Where the layout moves. |
| `rewire` | `"rewire": Window` | Crossfade for relationships rewired between surviving entities. |
| `step` | `"step": ScheduledStep` | The scheduled step these windows divide. |

### `sTurn`

```ts
sTurn(start: Point, end: Point, axis: Point, options?: RouteOptions): Turn | null | undefined
```

The geometry `sBend` draws, without drawing it.

### `subtitleMetrics`

```ts
subtitleMetrics: { "gap": 17; "line": 16; "lines": 3 }
```

A card's subtitle (see `GraphCanvasProps.subtitle`): human text under the label, `line` apart, its first baseline
`gap` under the text above it, on at most `lines` lines.

### `summaryChange`

```ts
summaryChange(was: number | undefined, now: number): Pick<SummaryFactItem, "added" | "removed">
```

A measure of each revision as a summary fact's changes: its net change between `was` and `now`, `added` when it
grew and `removed` when it shrank (`summaryChange(37826, 39882)` is `{added: 2056}`), nothing when it held or for
one extraction (`was` undefined).

### `SummaryCountItem`

```ts
interface SummaryCountItem
```

A count figure of the summary bar the host draws along every projection view: how many items of an extraction
`kind` (entity or relationship) there are, in the renderer's own word for them. `count` is the total in the
extraction, or in `after` for a comparison; `added`, `removed` and `modified` count the comparison's changes of that
status whose item has the kind (an added or modified change by its `after` item, a removed one by its `before` item),
and are omitted for one extraction. The previous total ("was N") is `count − added + removed`, so it is never sent.
`collection` tells an entity kind from a relationship kind of the same name. Hosts show their own counts of the
named kinds, so the counts are what the renderer checks verify; the vocabulary, and which kinds appear in what
order, are the renderer's. `type` is optional and defaults to `count`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `added` | `"added"?: number` | In a comparison, added items of the kind (by their `after` item). |
| `collection` | `"collection"?: "entities" \| "relationships"` | Which items `kind` names: entities or relationships. Absent, both (a kind that names either). |
| `count` | `"count": number` | Items of the kind in the extraction, or in `after` for a comparison; a non-negative integer. |
| `kind` | `"kind": string` | The extraction kind counted, 1 to `rendererLimits.summaryKind` characters; each kind once per collection. |
| `modified` | `"modified"?: number` | In a comparison, modified items of the kind (by their `after` item). |
| `noun` | `"noun": SummaryNoun` | The renderer's word for items of the kind. |
| `removed` | `"removed"?: number` | In a comparison, removed items of the kind (by their `before` item). |
| `type` | `"type"?: "count"` | Marks a count figure; the default when absent. |

### `SummaryFactContext`

```ts
interface SummaryFactContext
```

What a renderer's summary facts are computed from (`MountOptions.facts`): the document and its control values.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `controls` | `"controls": { [key: string]: false \| number \| string \| true }` | The value of every declared control, defaults filled in, for facts worded by a control (such as a measure). |
| `init` | `"init": RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } \| RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" }` | The host's `init` message: the extraction, or both revisions and their comparison. |
| `model` | `"model": ComparisonModel<Extraction>` | The shell's model of the document (`createModel`). |
| `rendererName` | `"rendererName": string` | The definition's renderer name (`init.projection.renderer`), for a bundle that presents several. |

### `SummaryFactItem`

```ts
interface SummaryFactItem
```

A fact figure of the summary bar: a finding of the renderer's domain that no kind count says, such as `2 breaking
changes` or `3 unprotected routes`. `id` is its stable key; `icon` names a theme icon token (`--projections-icon-<name>`,
none without it); `count` and `noun` are its words (singular for 1); `tone` colors the figure. With `ids`, the
entity or relationship IDs (or comparison change IDs) it is about, the figure filters to those items as a count
figure filters to its kind. In a comparison, `added`, `removed` and `modified` are its changes, which hosts draw
after it in the change colors as they draw a count figure's: how many of the things it counts arrived, left or
changed, or for a measure of each revision (`39,882 lines of code`) its net change, `added` when it grew and
`removed` when it shrank, so the previous value is `count − added + removed` as for a count. `description` is one
sentence of context hosts show as its tooltip and accessible description, such as the rules that decided it.
Hosts show a fact as the renderer sends it; the renderer checks verify its shape, that its `ids` exist and that a
single extraction's facts have no changes.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `added` | `"added"?: number` | In a comparison, how many of the counted things arrived, or a measure's net growth. |
| `count` | `"count": number` | The figure's number, a non-negative integer. |
| `description` | `"description"?: string` | One sentence of context, at most `rendererLimits.summaryDescription` characters, shown as the figure's tooltip. |
| `icon` | `"icon"?: string` | A theme icon token's name without its `icon-` prefix: a lowercase identifier; no icon when absent. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | Stable key, distinct among the summary's facts, 1 to `rendererLimits.summaryKind` characters. |
| `ids` | `"ids"?: Array<string>` | The items the fact is about, at most `rendererLimits.summaryFactIds`; activating the figure filters to them. |
| `modified` | `"modified"?: number` | In a comparison, how many of the counted things changed. |
| `noun` | `"noun": SummaryNoun` | The figure's words; `singular` for a `count` of 1, else `plural`. |
| `removed` | `"removed"?: number` | In a comparison, how many of the counted things left, or a measure's net shrinkage. |
| `tone` | `"tone"?: "added" \| "modified" \| "neutral" \| "removed"` | The figure's change color; absent or `neutral`, none. |
| `type` | `"type": "fact"` | Marks a fact figure. |

### `SummaryFacts`

```ts
type SummaryFacts = { (context: SummaryFactContext): Array<SummaryFactItem> }
```

A renderer's domain facts for the host's summary bar (`SummaryFactItem`): findings no kind count says, such as `2
breaking changes`, `1 enforcing rule +1` or `3 to replace`, computed from the document and the control values only,
so the bar is the same at every progress and in every pane. The shell posts them after the kind counts.

### `SummaryFactTone`

```ts
type SummaryFactTone = "added" | "modified" | "neutral" | "removed"
```

One of `summaryFactTones`: the change color of a fact's figure, or `neutral` for none.

### `SummaryItem`

```ts
type SummaryItem = SummaryCountItem | SummaryFactItem
```

One figure of the summary bar: a count of an extraction kind (`type: 'count'`, the default) or a domain fact
(`type: 'fact'`). Hosts drop an item of a `type` they don't know, keeping the rest, so new types stay additive.

### `SummaryNoun`

```ts
interface SummaryNoun
```

A noun of the renderer's domain, for one item and for any other count: `{singular: 'workspace', plural: 'workspaces'}`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `plural` | `"plural": string` | The word for zero or several items, 1 to `rendererLimits.summaryNoun` characters. |
| `singular` | `"singular": string` | The word for exactly one item, 1 to `rendererLimits.summaryNoun` characters. |

### `SummaryNouns`

```ts
type SummaryNouns = { (kind: string, collection: "entities" | "relationships"): SummaryNoun | false | undefined } | { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun | false }
```

A renderer's words for kinds: a noun per kind, or `false` to leave a kind out of the summary. A key may name one
collection's kind (`relationships:index`), which wins over the bare kind. As an object, the kinds it lists come
first, in its order; as a function (given the kind and its collection), `undefined` keeps the host's words.

### `summarySentence`

```ts
summarySentence(items: Array<{ "added"?: number | undefined; "count": number; "modified"?: number | undefined; "noun": SummaryNoun; "removed"?: number | undefined }>, locale?: string | undefined): string
```

The summary as one sentence, the same words the summary bar shows: `12 workspaces · 18 dependencies` for one
revision, `12 workspaces +1 −1 · 18 dependencies +2` for a comparison (changes that didn't happen are left out).

### `svgStatusWidth`

```ts
svgStatusWidth(parts: Array<StatusPart>, change?: undefined | { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }, textScale?: number): number
```

The width an SVG status line (`SvgChangeStatus`) takes with its words estimated rather than measured: per part an
icon, a gap and the word, parts a gap apart, then the volatile marker. A card reserves it so its status always
fits; `textScale` is the theme's extra-small type size over the default 12.

### `TableRow`

```ts
interface TableRow<T>
```

A table row: one item across a comparison, as the kit's model pairs it (`EntityChange`), or a snapshot's item.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after"?: T \| undefined` | The item in After; absent for a removal. |
| `before` | `"before"?: T \| undefined` | The item in Before; absent for an addition. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The row's selection ID, its `data-entity-id`. |
| `renamed` | `"renamed"?: false \| true \| undefined` | True when the item kept its identity under another ID. |
| `status` | `"status": "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "unchanged"` | The row's change: `unchanged` in a snapshot. |

### `TableSort`

```ts
type TableSort = null | { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" | "descending" }
```

The column a table is sorted by, and which way; `null` keeps the rows' own order.

### `tableSortControls`

```ts
tableSortControls<T>(options: TableSortControlsOptions<T>): Array<ControlBase & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } | ControlBase & { "default": false | true; "type": "toggle" } | ControlBase & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } | ControlBase & { "icon"?: "collapse" | "download" | "expand" | "filter" | "fit" | "next" | "previous" | "reset" | "search" | "settings" | "zoom-in" | "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>
```

A table's sort as renderer controls, which the host draws in its settings menu, remembers and lets agents read and
set: a choice of each sortable column in either direction (or the rows' own order), and a "Changes first" toggle.
Declare them (`MountOptions.controls`, or `declareControls`) and read them with `tableSortOf`; `DataTable` sets the
choice when a heading is activated (see `useTableProps`).


Options of `tableSortControls`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|

| `changesFirstDefault` | `"changesFirstDefault"?: false \| true` | The changes-first toggle's default; off unless set. |
| `columns` | `"columns": Array<SortableColumn<T>>` | The table's columns; each sortable one is offered both ways (24 at most). |

The box of a pill (see `pillMetrics`) around one line of text `advance` card units wide, its baseline at `baseline`,

```ts

```

A route without stretches shorter than half a unit (the slivers floating-point

How many step slots a schedule spans: one per step, plus its reading parts.
Report it with the step ends (`client.steps(ends, slots)`) so the host's
default pace gives every slot the same time, and reading never speeds up

```ts
trackSpacing: 10
```

### `TransitionEdge`

```ts
interface TransitionEdge extends EntityChange<Relationship>
```

One drawn relationship in a frame: the relationship row, its route and how present it is. A relationship too
faint to see, or with an endpoint the frame has no card for, is left out of the frame.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after"?: Relationship` | The item in the `after` extraction; absent for a removal and a further merged part. |
| `before` | `"before"?: Relationship` | The item in the `before` extraction; absent for an addition and a further split part. |
| `containment` | `"containment": false \| true` | A `contains` relationship from a compound boundary: drawn by the boundary enclosing its member, so it has no route (`points` is empty) and the canvas draws no link for it. |
| `context` | `"context"?: ChangeContext` | The comparison's `change.context`: the other items, by ID in each revision, a person needs to read the change. Absent for unchanged items and in a comparison saved without it; `changeContext` derives it from the structure then. |
| `correspondence` | `"correspondence"?: "declared" \| "exact" \| "merge" \| "none" \| "split"` | How the comparison matched `before` to `after`; absent in a snapshot (`snapshotChanges`). |
| `fromId` | `"fromId": string` | Entity row ID of the source, as used by `TransitionNode.id`. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The row's stable ID: the comparison change's ID, or the item's own ID for an item the comparison doesn't mention and for the further parts of a split or merge (suffixed `~1`, `~2`… only if that collides). |
| `key` | `"key": string` | Unique per drawn edge: a rewired relationship draws its old and new route separately. |
| `local` | `"local": number` | Progress through this relationship's own step, as `TransitionNode.local`. |
| `opacity` | `"opacity": number` | How present the route is, 0 to 1: never more than either endpoint's card, so it fades with what brings it. |
| `part` | `"part"?: "after" \| "before"` | Which revision's route of a rewired relationship this is, in the diff frame: its old route (removed) or its new one (added). Absent otherwise. |
| `points` | `"points": Array<Point>` | Route as a cubic Bézier chain (see `Spline`), on the same clock as its cards: from the source card's face to the target card's face. |
| `previousId` | `"previousId"?: string` | The `before` item's ID when `renamed`, for showing what it was called. |
| `renamed` | `"renamed"?: false \| true` | True when the item kept its identity under another ID (a `declared`, `split` or `merge` correspondence). |
| `shared` | `"shared": false \| true` | Routed through a shared-prerequisite junction (see `GraphLayoutOptions.junctions`). |
| `status` | `"status": "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "unchanged"` | The comparison's status for the item; `unchanged` for items it doesn't mention and in a snapshot. |
| `toId` | `"toId": string` | Entity row ID of the target, as used by `TransitionNode.id`. |
| `varied` | `"varied"?: Array<Varied>` | The comparison's `change.varied`: volatile values that differ between the two sides, each within its tolerance or beyond it. An `unchanged` row with `varied` varied only within tolerance and is presented as unchanged; a `modified` one with a value beyond tolerance carries the volatile marker (`variedBeyond`). |

### `TransitionNode`

```ts
interface TransitionNode extends EntityChange<Entity>, Point
```

One entity row's card or boundary in a frame: the row itself, its centre (`x`, `y`) and size in layout units, and
how present it is. A row too faint to see at this progress is left out of the frame.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after` | `"after"?: Entity` | The item in the `after` extraction; absent for a removal and a further merged part. |
| `before` | `"before"?: Entity` | The item in the `before` extraction; absent for an addition and a further split part. |
| `context` | `"context"?: ChangeContext` | The comparison's `change.context`: the other items, by ID in each revision, a person needs to read the change. Absent for unchanged items and in a comparison saved without it; `changeContext` derives it from the structure then. |
| `correspondence` | `"correspondence"?: "declared" \| "exact" \| "merge" \| "none" \| "split"` | How the comparison matched `before` to `after`; absent in a snapshot (`snapshotChanges`). |
| `group` | `"group": false \| true` | A compound module boundary rather than a card. |
| `height` | `"height": number` | The card's height, interpolated between the layouts the frame moves between. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | The row's stable ID: the comparison change's ID, or the item's own ID for an item the comparison doesn't mention and for the further parts of a split or merge (suffixed `~1`, `~2`… only if that collides). |
| `local` | `"local": number` | Progress through this row's own step, 0 before it starts and 1 after it ends; always 0 for a row no step changes. |
| `opacity` | `"opacity": number` | How present the card is, 0 to 1: fading in over its arrival window and out over its departure window. |
| `previousId` | `"previousId"?: string` | The `before` item's ID when `renamed`, for showing what it was called. |
| `renamed` | `"renamed"?: false \| true` | True when the item kept its identity under another ID (a `declared`, `split` or `merge` correspondence). |
| `status` | `"status": "added" \| "modified" \| "removed" \| "unchanged"` | The comparison's status for the item; `unchanged` for items it doesn't mention and in a snapshot. |
| `varied` | `"varied"?: Array<Varied>` | The comparison's `change.varied`: volatile values that differ between the two sides, each within its tolerance or beyond it. An `unchanged` row with `varied` varied only within tolerance and is presented as unchanged; a `modified` one with a value beyond tolerance carries the volatile marker (`variedBeyond`). |
| `width` | `"width": number` | The card's width, interpolated between the layouts the frame moves between. |
| `x` | `"x": number` | Distance rightward. |
| `y` | `"y": number` | Distance downward. |

### `Turn`

```ts
interface Turn
```

How an S turns: its middle along the axis (from `start`), radius and turn angle, or undefined for a straight route.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `across` | `"across": number` | Signed distance across the axis from start to finish. |
| `angle` | `"angle": number` | How far each turn bends, in radians: π/2 with a crossing run, less when a small offset makes the arcs meet. |
| `band` | `"band": readonly [number, number]` | Where the turns are confined, as distances from `start`. |
| `middle` | `"middle": number` | Where the S's middle (its crossing run) is, as a distance along the axis from `start`, inside `band`. |
| `radius` | `"radius": number` | The radius both turns share: `RouteOptions.radius` (default `routeRadius`), or less when the band is short. |

### `unitProgress`

```ts

```

Clamps progress to [0, 1], rejecting nonfinite values rather than guessing.

### `unscheduledWindow`

```ts
unscheduledWindow: Window
```

Window for rows a comparison does not place in any step.

### `variedBeyond`

```ts
variedBeyond(change: VariedChange): false | true
```

Whether a change is `modified` with a volatile value beyond its tolerance,
which presentations mark with the neutral `varied` icon beside the
change's status. A generated value regenerated from a changed basis isn't
one: it changed for a reason, which its field says (`generatedWords`).

### `variedBeyondLabel`

```ts
variedBeyondLabel: "Volatile field changed beyond tolerance"
```

The accessible name of the volatile marker (`variedBeyond`).

### `variedName`

```ts
variedName(path: string): string
```

A varied value's name for display: its pointer below `/data/`, segments
unescaped and joined with `/` (`/data/durationMs` is `durationMs`).

### `variedValue`

```ts
variedValue(item: unknown, path: string): unknown
```

The value a varied path (an RFC 6901 pointer into the item) points to, or `undefined`.

### `variedWithin`

```ts
variedWithin(change: VariedChange): false | true
```

Whether a change varied only within tolerance: `unchanged`, with `varied`.
Such an item is presented exactly as an unchanged one: no emphasis, status
or motion.

### `variedWords`

```ts
variedWords(within: false | true): string
```

How a varied value relates to its tolerance, in words: `within tolerance` or `beyond tolerance (volatile)`.

### `Window`

```ts
interface Window
```

A span of progress, centred on `time` and reaching `radius` either side: `[time - radius, time + radius]`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `radius` | `"radius": number` | Half the window's length, in progress; 0 for an instant. |
| `time` | `"time": number` | The window's centre, as progress from 0 (Before) to 1 (After). |

### `withDefinitionNouns`

```ts
withDefinitionNouns(items: Array<SummaryCountItem>, kinds: undefined | { [key: string]: RendererKind }): Array<SummaryCountItem>
```

Count figures worded with the definition's nouns (`presentation.kinds.<kind>.noun`, sent as
`init.projection.kinds`) where it gives one: a definition names its own kinds, so its words win over the
renderer's. Only the words change; which kinds appear, and their order, stay the renderer's.

### `within`

```ts
within(progress: number, start: number, end: number): number
```

Progress through a window `[start, end]`, clamped to [0, 1].

### `withSegments`

```ts
withSegments(points: Array<Point>, segments: number): Array<Point>
```

A chain with exactly `segments` segments drawing the same curve.

### `wrapText`

```ts
wrapText(text: string, limit: number): Array<string>
```

Data text shown whole on lines of at most `limit` characters: words fill
each line, and a word longer than a line breaks after the last `_ . / - , :`
that fits (so `aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm` reads `aws_cloudwatch_` then
`metric_alarm`), or, with none, at the limit. Nothing is dropped: joining
the lines gives the text back (spaces at a break are kept at the end of
their line). An empty text is one empty line.

### `zoomControls`

```ts
zoomControls: readonly [{ "group": "zoom"; "icon": "zoom-out"; "id": "zoom-out"; "label": "Zoom out"; "type": "action" }, { "group": "zoom"; "icon": "fit"; "id": "zoom-fit"; "label": "Fit to view"; "type": "action" }, { "group": "zoom"; "icon": "zoom-in"; "id": "zoom-in"; "label": "Zoom in"; "type": "action" }]
```

Zoom actions the host draws for a scalable stage (see `useStageZoom`); pass
them as `mountRenderer(…, {controls: zoomControls})`. Pinch and Ctrl/⌘-wheel
zoom stay in the frame, and the stage scrolls to pan.

### `zoomLimits`

```ts
zoomLimits: { "max": number; "readable": number; "step": number }
```

Zoom as a multiple of the fitted scale: 1 fits everything (the minimum, and
the opening view unless that draws text below `openingFloorPx`), each Zoom in or out multiplies or divides by `step`, and
the most is `max` times the fit or `readable` (CSS px per content unit),
whichever is larger, so a fit too small to read can always be zoomed to a
legible size.

## React (`@githubnext/projections/kit/react`)

### `Badge`

```ts
Badge(__0: { "emphasis"?: number; "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }): Element | null
```

Change badges, faded by emphasis. At zero emphasis they render nothing, so
endpoints carry no change decoration and release the badge's footprint.

### `CardChangeMarks`

```ts
CardChangeMarks(__0: { "change": { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }; "classification": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "renamed" | "unchanged"; "emphasis": number; "fill"?: false | true; "footer"?: number; "height": number; "inset": number; "parts"?: Array<StatusPart> | undefined; "width": number; "x": number; "y": number }): Element | null
```

A changed card's marks, as every kit card draws them: the card filled with its change's soft hue under a strong
edge of the same hue (inset by `inset`, see `emphasisInset`, with its radius less the inset, so it is concentric with
the card's border), and a footer band `footer` tall across its bottom, ruled off from the body, holding the status
words centred (see `SvgChangeStatus`). The band is clipped to the card's shape (`node-card-shape`, rounded as the
card's surface is), so its corners follow the card's, and the edge is drawn again over it, so the band never covers
the border or pokes outside its corners. Draw it over the card's surface and under its text;
everything fades with `emphasis`, and nothing is drawn at zero. `fill: false` leaves the body's fill to the
caller, for a card whose parts tint their own slices of it.

The box is in card units: `x` and `y` are its top-left corner.

### `cardCornerRadius`

```ts
cardCornerRadius: 6
```

The corner radius a graph card's shape is drawn with, in card units, where the theme's radius (`rx` in CSS,
`--projections-radius`) doesn't reach: a shape's CSS `rx` wins over it.

Cards in a responsive grid: as many columns as fit, one on a phone.


The renderer's content root: scrolls as the host's main view (`data-projections-scroll`) and starts at the top of
