gets the same by giving it the class `pk-stage`.

### `DataTable`

```ts
DataTable<T>(__0: DataTableProps<T>): Element
```

A data table: a row per item and a column per property, the first column frozen when it scrolls sideways, every
heading a button that sorts by its column. In a comparison each row keeps one place for the whole transition
(sorted by After's version, Before's for a removed row), a status column says its change in words, and changed cells
are value changes: was and now pills in the diff, tinted by emphasis in the progress modes. An added or removed row
is marked as a whole; a row around changed cells stays neutral. Every boundary is one line, which takes the change's
hue when the row on either side of it is changed. Rows are selectable units (`data-entity-id`). Pass the sort and
`onSortChange` from `useTableProps` to keep it in the host's controls (`tableSortControls`), or leave them out for a
table that doesn't sort.

### `DataTableColumn`

```ts
interface DataTableColumn<T> extends SortableColumn<T>
```

One column of a `DataTable`: its heading, what its cells show and how it sorts.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `align` | `"align"?: "end" \| "start"` | The cells' alignment: `end` for numbers (the default for a numeric `sort`), else `start`. |
| `changed` | `"changed"?: { (before: T, after: T): false \| true }` | Whether the cell changed between a row's two versions: drawn as a value change (was, now) in the diff and tinted in the progress modes. By default, whether `value` differs. |
| `firstDirection` | `"firstDirection"?: "ascending" \| "descending"` | The direction a first click on the heading sorts in; `ascending` by default. |
| `font` | `"font"?: "code" \| "text"` | `code` for identifiers and other symbols (names, paths, versions), in the monospace font; `text` (default) for words. |
| `id` | `"id": string` | Stable ID: letters, digits, `_`, `.` and `-`, at most 48 characters. It names the column in the sort control. |
| `label` | `"label": string` | The column's heading, in words. |
| `render` | `"render"?: { (item: T): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> \| Promise<Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> \| ReactElement<unknown, string \| { (props: any): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> \| Promise \| Promise<ReactNode> \| ReactElement<unknown, recursive> \| ReactPortal \| bigint \| false \| null \| number \| string \| true \| undefined } \| { new (props: any, context: any): Component<any, any, any> }> \| ReactPortal \| bigint \| false \| null \| number \| string \| true \| undefined> \| ReactElement<unknown, string \| { (props: any): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> \| Promise<Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> \| ReactElement<unknown, recursive> \| ReactPortal \| bigint \| false \| null \| number \| string \| true \| undefined> \| Promise<ReactNode> \| ReactElement \| ReactPortal \| bigint \| false \| null \| number \| string \| true \| undefined } \| { new (props: any, context: any): Component<any, any, any> }> \| ReactPortal \| bigint \| false \| null \| number \| string \| true \| undefined }` | A cell's content for one version of a row; the formatted `value` by default. |
| `sort` | `"sort"?: "number" \| "string" \| false \| { (a: T, b: T): number }` | How the column orders rows (see `ColumnSort`). |
| `value` | `"value"?: { (item: T): false \| null \| number \| string \| true \| undefined }` | The cell's value in one version of a row: what the column sorts by, and shows unless the column renders its own. |
| `width` | `"width"?: "fill" \| "fit"` | `fill` takes the width the table has to spare (the first column's default); `fit` (the others') fits the content. |

### `DataTableProps`

```ts
interface DataTableProps<T>
```

Props of `DataTable`.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `changesFirst` | `"changesFirst"?: false \| true` | Changed rows before the rest. |
| `columns` | `"columns": Array<DataTableColumn<T>>` | The columns, in order; the first is the row's heading, frozen when the table scrolls sideways. |
| `comparing` | `"comparing"?: false \| true` | A comparison: a status column says each row's change in words. |
| `diff` | `"diff"?: false \| true` | Diff mode: both versions at once, changed values as was/now pills and added and removed rows marked. |
| `emphasis` | `"emphasis"?: { (row: TableRow<T>): number }` | A row's change emphasis (`RendererProps.emphasis`): 0 at both endpoints and before its step. |
| `frozen` | `"frozen"?: false \| true` | Keep the first column in view when the table scrolls sideways; on by default. |
| `label` | `"label": string` | The table's accessible name, such as what its rows are. |
| `locale` | `"locale"?: string` | BCP 47 locale for numbers and comparing strings (`RendererProps.locale`). |
| `noun` | `"noun"?: string` | The rows' plural noun, for a fold's words ("12 unchanged languages"); `rows` by default. |
| `onSelect` | `"onSelect"?: { (id: string): void }` | Selects a row (`RendererProps.onSelect`), when its heading is activated. |
| `onSortChange` | `"onSortChange"?: { (sort: { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" \| "descending" }): void }` | A heading was activated: the sort it asks for. Without it, headings don't sort. |
| `progress` | `"progress"?: number` | The frame's progress, 0 (Before) to 1 (After), outside diff mode: each row shows the version it has reached. |
| `rowProgress` | `"rowProgress"?: { (row: TableRow<T>): number }` | A row's progress through its own step (a staged timeline's `local`), for rows that change at different times. |
| `rows` | `"rows": Array<TableRow<T>>` | The rows, in their own order (kept while unsorted): the kit's model rows (`model.entities`) or rows like them. |
| `scope` | `"scope"?: ChangesScope \| undefined` | The Changes scope (`RendererProps.scope`): each run of rows it doesn't show, in the sorted order, folds into one row that opens in place. |
| `selectedId` | `"selectedId"?: null \| string` | The host's selection (`RendererProps.selectedId`). |
| `sort` | `"sort"?: null \| { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" \| "descending" }` | The sort; the rows' own order when `null` or absent. |

The kit's arrowhead (see `arrowHead`) as an SVG marker, for paths that end

### `EntityCard`


One entity as a card: a unit the host rings on hover, focus and selection, a button that selects it, its name and
identifier, and its change status in words, in space that is always reserved. In the progress modes its edge takes
the change's hue as the step emphasizes it; in diff mode (`mark`) it is filled and edged like any kit region.

### `GeneratedMark`

```ts
GeneratedMark(): Element
```

The quiet mark beside every generated field's name: the `generated` icon and the word "Generated", muted, so a
summary is never mistaken for an extracted fact. A field label, never a change badge.

### `GeneratedText`

```ts
GeneratedText(__0: { "after"?: unknown; "bases"?: { "after"?: Readonly<Record<string, string>>; "before"?: Readonly<Record<string, string>> }; "before"?: unknown; "entry"?: Pick<Varied, "because" | "generated" | "reason" | "within"> | undefined; "name": string }): Element
```

A generated field: its name, the Generated mark and its value, in the form its change calls for.

- No change (`entry` absent): the value.
- Regenerated from the same inputs (`entry.within`): After's text, the neutral `varied` icon and "Regenerated from
  the same inputs", with a toggle that shows Before's wording in place. Never a word diff: rewording from the same
  inputs carries no information.
- Regenerated because its basis changed: why, then Before and After as whole passages side by side (stacked when
  narrow), with a "Word diff" toggle for strings.

Toggling never shifts layout: both forms share one grid cell. `bases` lets a moved model read with its old and
new IDs.

### `GraphAnchor`

```ts
interface GraphAnchor
```

The card a person activated to change the view, and what stands in its place in the next view: the same card, or
the one that replaces it (the boundary a summary card expands into). When the next view is laid out, the canvas keeps
the zoom, keeps `to`'s top left corner where `from`'s was on screen, and moves the cards from where they were to
where they go while the cards the view reveals fade in.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `from` | `"from": string` | The activated card's ID, in the view drawn when it was activated. |
| `to` | `"to": string` | The ID of what stands in its place in the next view. |

### `GraphCanvas`

```ts
GraphCanvas(props: GraphCanvasProps): Element
```

The staged graph canvas shared by the graph, DAG and architecture renderers:
ELK layouts per comparison step (laid out off the main thread before the
first paint), identity-stable cards, spline relationships that morph on the
same clock as their cards, stable framing across the whole transition, and
host-driven change emphasis.

### `graphCanvasControls`

```ts
graphCanvasControls: readonly [{ "group": "zoom"; "icon": "zoom-out"; "id": "zoom-out"; "label": "Zoom out"; "type": "action" }, { "group": "zoom"; "icon": "fit"; "id": "zoom-fit"; "label": "Fit to view"; "type": "action" }, { "group": "zoom"; "icon": "zoom-in"; "id": "zoom-in"; "label": "Zoom in"; "type": "action" }]
```

Zoom actions the host draws for a `GraphCanvas` (the kit's `zoomControls`);
pass them as `mountRenderer(…, {controls: graphCanvasControls})`. The canvas
opens fitted, everything in view, unless that draws text below the kit's
`openingFloorPx`: then it opens at that floor on its top row and scrolls.
Pinch and Ctrl/⌘-wheel zoom stay in the frame, and a zoomed canvas scrolls
to pan.

### `graphCanvasPace`

```ts
graphCanvasPace: { "stepMs": number }
```

The playback pace graph canvases read best at, for `capabilities.pace`:
cards travel and fade over most of each step, which needs time to follow.

### `GraphCanvasProps`

```ts
interface GraphCanvasProps extends RendererProps<undefined>
```

Props of `GraphCanvas`: the renderer's own props, passed through, and how the graph lays out and labels its cards.
Everything but the renderer props is optional; the defaults draw every entity as a card of its kind.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `accent` | `"accent"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): CardAccent \| undefined }` | A card's accent: a band in its paint along the card's leading edge, its meaning in the card's accessible name. |
| `anchor` | `"anchor"?: GraphAnchor \| undefined` | What the next view of the same document (`source`) keeps in place, when the person changed the view by activating a card, such as a summary card that expands its group: see `GraphAnchor`. Pass a new object for each activation. |
| `badges` | `"badges"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): Array<string \| { "prose"?: true; "text": string; "tone"?: "highlight" \| "quiet" }> \| undefined }` | Short facts drawn as badges in rows under a card's text, such as a data field's values: the card grows a row for each row of badges either revision needs. They crossfade with the card's own step when they change; in the diff, badges a modified card gained or lost are marked added or removed. A badge is code, in monospace (`network`), or `{text, prose: true}` for human words, in sans (`property tests`). Pass a stable function: a new one lays out again. |
| `changedFields` | `"changedFields"?: undefined \| { (row: EntityChange<Entity>): Array<FieldLine> \| undefined }` | Diff mode's field changes of a modified entity, drawn inline on its card (the name, then the old value struck through and the new one), which grows to hold them: at most three, then a count of the rest. Values are shown verbatim and whole (see `diffCardText`). |
| `colorMode` | `"colorMode": "dark" \| "light"` | The host theme's color mode, for colors a renderer computes itself (see `categoryPalette`). |
| `comparing` | `"comparing": false \| true` | Whether this is a comparison (`init.mode === 'comparison'`). |
| `comparisonMode` | `"comparisonMode": "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe" \| undefined` | The comparison mode the host announced in `init`, if any. |
| `compound` | `"compound"?: Array<string> \| false \| true` | Group containment-only entities into boundaries: `true` for modules (architecture), or the kinds that may become boundaries. |
| `controls` | `"controls": { [key: string]: false \| number \| string \| true }` | The value of every declared control (from `MountOptions.controls` or `declareControls`), defaults filled in. The host draws the controls and sends their values; renderers draw no settings controls of their own. |
| `declareControls` | `"declareControls": { (controls: Array<ControlBase & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } \| ControlBase & { "default": false \| true; "type": "toggle" } \| ControlBase & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } \| ControlBase & { "icon"?: "collapse" \| "download" \| "expand" \| "filter" \| "fit" \| "next" \| "previous" \| "reset" \| "search" \| "settings" \| "zoom-in" \| "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>): void }` | Replaces the declared controls, for controls that depend on the document (for example a filter listing its kinds). Repeated identical declarations are ignored. |
| `declareNouns` | `"declareNouns": { (nouns: undefined \| { (kind: string, collection: "entities" \| "relationships"): SummaryNoun \| false \| undefined } \| { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun \| false }): void }` | Names the document's kinds in the host's summary bar, replacing `MountOptions.nouns` (see `useSummaryNouns`). The shell counts every kind and posts the summary itself; without nouns, the host words kinds from their names. |
| `describeStatus` | `"describeStatus"?: undefined \| { (node: TransitionNode): Array<StatusPart> \| undefined }` | The domain's wording of a row's change in its status footer and accessible name (see `StatusPart`). |
| `detail` | `"detail"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): string \| undefined }` | A short code identifier drawn in monospace at the right of a card's kind line, such as a package version. When it differs between revisions, the two crossfade with the card's own step. |
| `diff` | `"diff": false \| true` | Whether the host presents this comparison in `diff` mode: one static frame showing both subjects, with no progress (`progress` stays 1 and `schedule` is empty). Draw the renderer's own static comparison; `highlighting` is the host's change emphasis for it (1 unless the host turned highlighting off). |
| `direction` | `"direction": -1 \| 1` | The host's playback direction (`ProgressPayload.direction`): 1 toward After, -1 back toward Before. Always 1 for an extraction and in diff mode. `schedule` is already ordered for the direction the transition presents. |
| `emphasis` | `"emphasis": EmphasisOf` | A change's emphasis now: 0 until its comparison step begins, then the host's highlighting; in a held pane, the host's highlighting (see `stepEmphasis`). Pass the row ID as the second argument when the object passed has none. |
| `environment` | `"environment": RendererEnvironment` | The host's current theme, motion preference, locale and pane: `init`'s, or a later `environment`'s. |
| `filtered` | `"filtered"?: false \| true \| undefined` | Whether the host has said what it shows (its filter, and with it the scope). Until it does, every item is drawn, provisionally: a canvas that moves between layouts of the scope doesn't move from that one, so the first scope the host chooses is drawn at once rather than pared down to. Undefined where no host filter is wired (treat it as said). |
| `focus` | `"focus"?: undefined \| { "ids": ReadonlySet<string>; "label": string }` | Entity rows to bring forward, for example what depends on the selection: other cards and relationships recede. `label` says what is highlighted, for people who don't see the graph. |
| `focusRequest` | `"focusRequest": RendererFocus \| undefined` | Where the host wants the opening view (`InitPayload.focus`), or a comparison's changes while the host shows changes only; undefined for the renderer's own choice. The shell scrolls the first focused item of a list into view itself; a renderer that places its own view (`useStageZoom`) frames what it names. |
| `highlighting` | `"highlighting": number` | Host-chosen change emphasis, exactly 0 at both endpoints and for extractions. Use `emphasis(row)` for a change's own emphasis: it is scoped to the change's step. |
| `hoveredId` | `"hoveredId": null \| string` | The entity the host says is hovered, in this frame or another pane, or `null`. The shell already marks its elements with `data-projections-hovered`; use this only for richer hover presentation. |
| `icon` | `"icon"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): string \| undefined }` | A small icon before a card's kind line, and before a boundary's heading, that says at a glance what the entity is: a name in `cardIconNames` (Lucide's, such as `terminal` or `database`), drawn 14 units square in the muted text color. Any other name draws nothing, so a renderer may pass a data field's value as it is; the kind line keeps room for the icon wherever either revision has one. A changed icon crossfades with the card's own step; the diff shows the After revision's. Pass a stable function: a new one lays out again. |
| `init` | `"init": RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": Extraction; "before": Extraction; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } \| RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": Extraction; "mode": "extraction" }` | The host's `init` message as received: the extraction, or both revisions and their comparison. |
| `kindLine` | `"kindLine"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): KindLineText \| undefined }` | A card's kind line (and a boundary's heading) instead of the entity's kind, for example a resource type. `identifier` draws it in the monospace font; a long one keeps its end, the most specific part. `note` follows it in the text font (`aws_db_instance · Replace`). |
| `locale` | `"locale": string` | BCP 47 locale for formatting numbers and dates, for example `en-US`. |
| `model` | `"model": ComparisonModel<Extraction>` | `init` resolved for presentation (see `createModel`): rows keyed by identity, built once per document. |
| `onAction` | `"onAction": { (listener: { (id: string): void }): { (): void } }` | Subscribes to the host's `action` messages for declared action controls; returns an unsubscribe function. |
| `onOpen` | `"onOpen": { (path: string, line?: number \| undefined): void }` | Ask the host to navigate to source evidence; the host decides. |
| `onSelect` | `"onSelect": { (id: null \| string): void }` | Selects an item, as the person activating it: activating the selected item again clears the selection, as an `aria-pressed` toggle does, and `null` clears it. The shell also clears the selection when the person clicks the renderer's background, and toggles an item when they click its element anywhere outside a control. |
| `options` | `"options": RendererOptions` | The host's latest `options`, such as `showRelationships`; empty until it sends any. |
| `orientation` | `"orientation"?: "horizontal" \| "vertical"` | The layers' direction: `vertical` (the default) runs top to bottom, `horizontal` left to right. |
| `pane` | `"pane": "after" \| "before" \| undefined` | Set while this frame is one held pane of side by side or swipe (`RendererEnvironment.pane`): it shows only that revision, which the host labels, so leave out narration of the transition such as step captions. |
| `progress` | `"progress": number` | 0 (before) to 1 (after); always 1 for an extraction. |
| `prose` | `"prose"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): false \| true }` | Cards whose label is human language rather than an identifier (for example a summary card), drawn in sans. |
| `reducedMotion` | `"reducedMotion": false \| true` | Whether the person prefers reduced motion: present each frame without decorative movement. |
| `relationshipColor` | `"relationshipColor"?: undefined \| { (relationship: Relationship): string \| undefined }` | A relationship's paint while its change isn't emphasized, such as a color per relationship kind. |
| `rendererName` | `"rendererName": string` | Definition renderer name the host matched, for example `graph-horizontal`. |
| `reportLegend` | `"reportLegend": { (legend: RendererLegend): void }` | Reports the legend the host draws once beside every pane (an empty one clears it). Renderers draw no legend of their own; repeated identical legends are ignored. |
| `reportSteps` | `"reportSteps": { (ends: Array<number>, slots?: number \| undefined): void }` | Report step boundaries where a host may hold, for renderers with their own timing, and optionally how many step slots the presentation spans (`timelineSlots`). |
| `requestDocument` | `"requestDocument": { (name: string): Promise<string> }` | Asks the host for a built-in renderer's document, to run nested (`embedRenderer`); rejects with the host's reason when it supplies none (see `RendererClient.requestDocument`). |
| `schedule` | `"schedule": Array<ScheduledStep>` | The comparison's steps on the progress axis for the direction this transition presents (see `DirectionLatch`). Empty for extractions. |
| `scope` | `"scope": ScopeView \| undefined` | The Changes scope, while the host shows a comparison's changes and their context (`changesScope`): its `shown` items, with the parts the person opened (`expand`). A list folds the rest (`useFolds`, `Fold`); a canvas that declares `MountOptions.scope` `subset` receives a `model` of only what is shown and lays that out. Nothing is faded: what is shown is drawn at full strength, and what isn't takes no room. Undefined while every item is shown. |
| `selectedId` | `"selectedId": null \| string` | The selected item's ID (an entity row ID, or a part's `data-entity-id`), or `null` when nothing is selected. |
| `setControl` | `"setControl": { (id: string, value: false \| number \| string \| true): void }` | Sets a declared control from the renderer's own content, as the person changed it there (a sortable column header): the host applies it as if they had set it in its settings, remembers it and sends it back in `controls`. The new value shows at once. |
| `source` | `"source"?: unknown` | What `model` is a view of, when a renderer derives it (for example with groups expanded or collapsed): while a new model of the same document is laid out, the current layout stays on screen, and keyboard focus with it, instead of the loading state. |
| `subtitle` | `"subtitle"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): string \| undefined }` | A few words under a card's label, such as what the entity is for: human text in sans, wrapped to the card on at most `subtitleMetrics.lines` lines and ending in an ellipsis when longer (the tooltip has it whole). The card grows a line for each line either revision needs; a changed one crossfades with the card's own step. Pass a stable function: a new one lays out again. |
| `synthetic` | `"synthetic"?: undefined \| { (id: string): false \| true }` | Presentation-only cards and links that stand for no extracted entity or relationship, such as a summary of collapsed items: drawn and activated (through `onSelect`) like the others, but carrying no selection ID (`data-graph-synthetic` instead of `data-entity-id`), so hosts never see them. |
| `syntheticAction` | `"syntheticAction"?: undefined \| { (entity: Entity): undefined \| { "expanded"?: false \| true; "label": string } }` | A synthetic card's accessible name and, for one that opens or closes a group of cards, whether that group is open (`aria-expanded`). Defaults to `Show` and the card's label. |
| `viewport` | `"viewport": undefined \| { "height": number; "width": number }` | The frame's width and the host window's height, CSS px, as the host last reported them; undefined until then. |
| `visibleIds` | `"visibleIds"?: ReadonlySet<string> \| undefined` | Entity rows to present, for example after a search; defaults to every row. |

### `graphEntityLimit`

```ts
graphEntityLimit: 500
```

Most entities a graph lays out; beyond this the canvas asks for a narrower view.

### `Group`

```ts
Group(__0: GroupProps): Element
```

A titled panel: a raised, edged unit whose header band, inside its edge, names what it holds, then its body. The
band holds the subject's `icon`, if any, the title (`titleFont="code"` when the title is code), muted `meta`, any
`actions` and, in a comparison, the item's `change` in words at its end; a group marked removed in the diff strikes
its title through. With `id` the group presents a selectable item, ringed by the SDK over its own edge, and its title
is the button that selects it.
The body is flush with the group's sides, so a table's rows run edge to edge; the group clips them to its corners.

### `KitRenderer`


Connects a kit renderer component to its host through the renderer frame protocol.

### `MountOptions`

```ts
interface MountOptions
```

How `mountRenderer` connects a renderer component to its host.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `accepts` | `"accepts"?: Array<RendererAccepts>` | The extractions the renderer presents, the same list its `vite.config.ts` passes to `rendererConfig`. An extraction outside it shows a failure naming what the renderer accepts. Omit it to accept any. |
| `capabilities` | `"capabilities": RendererCapabilities` | What the renderer supports, declared to the host in `ready` (see `RendererCapabilities`); the shell adds the interaction capabilities unless `interactions` is `false`. |
| `controls` | `"controls"?: Array<ControlBase & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } \| ControlBase & { "default": false \| true; "type": "toggle" } \| ControlBase & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } \| ControlBase & { "icon"?: "collapse" \| "download" \| "expand" \| "filter" \| "fit" \| "next" \| "previous" \| "reset" \| "search" \| "settings" \| "zoom-in" \| "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>` | Controls the host draws for this renderer, declared in `ready` (see `declareControls` for document-dependent ones). |
| `facts` | `"facts"?: SummaryFacts` | The renderer's domain facts for the host's summary bar (`SummaryFacts`), computed from the document and the control values whenever either changes, and posted after the kind counts. A renderer draws no summary line of its own: what it would count goes here. |
| `interactions` | `"interactions"?: false` | Hover, anchors, scroll mirroring, the host's filter and annotation badges through `connectInteractions` over elements carrying `data-entity-id` (default on). `false` opts out and declares none of the interaction capabilities. |
| `name` | `"name": string` | Bundle name, used for `data-renderer` on the root element. |
| `nouns` | `"nouns"?: { (kind: string, collection: "entities" \| "relationships"): SummaryNoun \| false \| undefined } \| { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun \| false }` | The renderer's words for extraction kinds in the host's summary bar (`SummaryNouns`), for every document; see `declareNouns` for words that depend on the document. |
| `scope` | `"scope"?: { "context"?: { (all: ComparisonModel<Extraction>, changes: ReadonlySet<string>, renderer: string): Iterable<string, any, any> }; "layout": "subset"; "parts"?: "fold" \| "omit" \| "whole" } \| { "layout": "fold" }` | How the Changes scope reaches the renderer. `fold` (the default): `model` holds every item and the renderer folds what `scope` leaves out, as a list does. `subset`: `model` holds only what the scope shows (`scopedModel`), with the shown entities' `parts` left out, kept whole or folded, so a canvas lays out only that; `scope.all` holds every item. A subset renderer that needs more to place a change than its relationships' endpoints and containers (a package's path from the workspace, a selector's probe and hook) returns those items' row IDs from `context`, given every item, the changes in scope and its renderer name; they show as context. |
| `steps` | `"steps"?: "manual" \| "schedule"` | `schedule` (default) reports the end of each scheduled step to the host; `manual` leaves it to the component through `reportSteps`. |

### `mountRenderer`

```ts
mountRenderer<A extends Array<RendererAccepts> | undefined = undefined>(component: ComponentClass<RendererProps<NoInfer<A>>, any> | FunctionComponent<RendererProps<NoInfer<A>>>, options: MountOptions & { "accepts"?: A }): { "unmount"(): void }
```

Mounts a kit renderer into the bundle's `#root`, from the renderer's entry
module (`rendererConfig({view})` generates one that calls it). Mounting again
in the same document, as a development server's hot update re-runs the
entry, first unmounts the earlier renderer. No StrictMode: its doubled
effects would connect to the host, and post `ready`, twice.

One pill of a `ChangePills` list.

### `Prose`

```ts
Prose(__0: { "children": string }): Element
```

Human-readable protocol text (a reason, summary, notice, diagnostic or
detail) whose backtick-delimited spans are inline code, as the contracts
define: each span is drawn as a code identifier (monospace, marked
`data-projections-identifier`), the rest in the text font. Text is never
inserted as HTML. For a title, label or assistive text, use `plainProse`.

### `RelationshipItem`


A relationship as a row: an item of its own, marked with its ID, selectable and focusable. In the progress modes it

change to assistive technology.

### `RendererExtraction`

```ts
type RendererExtraction<T extends "api/v0" | "architecture/v0" | "dag/v0" | "database/v0" | "graph/v0" | "metrics/v0" | "treemap/v0" | Array<RendererAccepts> | undefined> = T extends "graph/v0" | "dag/v0" | "treemap/v0" | "metrics/v0" | "api/v0" | "database/v0" | "architecture/v0" ? ExtractionOf<T, never> : T extends readonly RendererAccepts[] ? AcceptedExtraction<T> : Extraction
```

The extraction type a renderer receives: `RendererProps<'database/v0'>` types a renderer of one domain
schema, `RendererProps<typeof accepts>` one that accepts several or a vocabulary, and `RendererProps` one
of any extraction.

### `RendererProps`

```ts
interface RendererProps<T extends "api/v0" | "architecture/v0" | "dag/v0" | "database/v0" | "graph/v0" | "metrics/v0" | "treemap/v0" | Array<RendererAccepts> | undefined = undefined>
```

Everything a kit renderer component receives for one host state.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `colorMode` | `"colorMode": "dark" \| "light"` | The host theme's color mode, for colors a renderer computes itself (see `categoryPalette`). |
| `comparing` | `"comparing": false \| true` | Whether this is a comparison (`init.mode === 'comparison'`). |
| `comparisonMode` | `"comparisonMode": "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe" \| undefined` | The comparison mode the host announced in `init`, if any. |
| `controls` | `"controls": { [key: string]: false \| number \| string \| true }` | The value of every declared control (from `MountOptions.controls` or `declareControls`), defaults filled in. The host draws the controls and sends their values; renderers draw no settings controls of their own. |
| `declareControls` | `"declareControls": { (controls: Array<ControlBase & { "choices": Array<{ "label": string; "value": string }>; "default": string; "type": "choice" } \| ControlBase & { "default": false \| true; "type": "toggle" } \| ControlBase & { "default": number; "max": number; "min": number; "step": number; "type": "range"; "unit"?: string } \| ControlBase & { "icon"?: "collapse" \| "download" \| "expand" \| "filter" \| "fit" \| "next" \| "previous" \| "reset" \| "search" \| "settings" \| "zoom-in" \| "zoom-out"; "type": "action" }>): void }` | Replaces the declared controls, for controls that depend on the document (for example a filter listing its kinds). Repeated identical declarations are ignored. |
| `declareNouns` | `"declareNouns": { (nouns: undefined \| { (kind: string, collection: "entities" \| "relationships"): SummaryNoun \| false \| undefined } \| { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun \| false }): void }` | Names the document's kinds in the host's summary bar, replacing `MountOptions.nouns` (see `useSummaryNouns`). The shell counts every kind and posts the summary itself; without nouns, the host words kinds from their names. |
| `diff` | `"diff": false \| true` | Whether the host presents this comparison in `diff` mode: one static frame showing both subjects, with no progress (`progress` stays 1 and `schedule` is empty). Draw the renderer's own static comparison; `highlighting` is the host's change emphasis for it (1 unless the host turned highlighting off). |
| `direction` | `"direction": -1 \| 1` | The host's playback direction (`ProgressPayload.direction`): 1 toward After, -1 back toward Before. Always 1 for an extraction and in diff mode. `schedule` is already ordered for the direction the transition presents. |
| `emphasis` | `"emphasis": EmphasisOf` | A change's emphasis now: 0 until its comparison step begins, then the host's highlighting; in a held pane, the host's highlighting (see `stepEmphasis`). Pass the row ID as the second argument when the object passed has none. |
| `environment` | `"environment": RendererEnvironment` | The host's current theme, motion preference, locale and pane: `init`'s, or a later `environment`'s. |
| `filtered` | `"filtered"?: false \| true \| undefined` | Whether the host has said what it shows (its filter, and with it the scope). Until it does, every item is drawn, provisionally: a canvas that moves between layouts of the scope doesn't move from that one, so the first scope the host chooses is drawn at once rather than pared down to. Undefined where no host filter is wired (treat it as said). |
| `focusRequest` | `"focusRequest": RendererFocus \| undefined` | Where the host wants the opening view (`InitPayload.focus`), or a comparison's changes while the host shows changes only; undefined for the renderer's own choice. The shell scrolls the first focused item of a list into view itself; a renderer that places its own view (`useStageZoom`) frames what it names. |
| `highlighting` | `"highlighting": number` | Host-chosen change emphasis, exactly 0 at both endpoints and for extractions. Use `emphasis(row)` for a change's own emphasis: it is scoped to the change's step. |
| `hoveredId` | `"hoveredId": null \| string` | The entity the host says is hovered, in this frame or another pane, or `null`. The shell already marks its elements with `data-projections-hovered`; use this only for richer hover presentation. |
| `init` | `"init": RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "after": RendererExtraction<T>; "before": RendererExtraction<T>; "comparison": Comparison; "comparisonMode"?: "animated" \| "diff" \| "side-by-side" \| "swipe"; "mode": "comparison" } \| RendererEnvironment & { "focus"?: RendererFocus; "projection": RendererProjection } & { "extraction": RendererExtraction<T>; "mode": "extraction" }` | The host's `init` message as received: the extraction, or both revisions and their comparison. |
| `locale` | `"locale": string` | BCP 47 locale for formatting numbers and dates, for example `en-US`. |
| `model` | `"model": ComparisonModel<RendererExtraction<T>>` | `init` resolved for presentation (see `createModel`): rows keyed by identity, built once per document. |
| `onAction` | `"onAction": { (listener: { (id: string): void }): { (): void } }` | Subscribes to the host's `action` messages for declared action controls; returns an unsubscribe function. |
| `onOpen` | `"onOpen": { (path: string, line?: number \| undefined): void }` | Ask the host to navigate to source evidence; the host decides. |
| `onSelect` | `"onSelect": { (id: null \| string): void }` | Selects an item, as the person activating it: activating the selected item again clears the selection, as an `aria-pressed` toggle does, and `null` clears it. The shell also clears the selection when the person clicks the renderer's background, and toggles an item when they click its element anywhere outside a control. |
| `options` | `"options": RendererOptions` | The host's latest `options`, such as `showRelationships`; empty until it sends any. |
| `pane` | `"pane": "after" \| "before" \| undefined` | Set while this frame is one held pane of side by side or swipe (`RendererEnvironment.pane`): it shows only that revision, which the host labels, so leave out narration of the transition such as step captions. |
| `progress` | `"progress": number` | 0 (before) to 1 (after); always 1 for an extraction. |
| `reducedMotion` | `"reducedMotion": false \| true` | Whether the person prefers reduced motion: present each frame without decorative movement. |
| `rendererName` | `"rendererName": string` | Definition renderer name the host matched, for example `graph-horizontal`. |
| `reportLegend` | `"reportLegend": { (legend: RendererLegend): void }` | Reports the legend the host draws once beside every pane (an empty one clears it). Renderers draw no legend of their own; repeated identical legends are ignored. |
| `reportSteps` | `"reportSteps": { (ends: Array<number>, slots?: number \| undefined): void }` | Report step boundaries where a host may hold, for renderers with their own timing, and optionally how many step slots the presentation spans (`timelineSlots`). |
| `requestDocument` | `"requestDocument": { (name: string): Promise<string> }` | Asks the host for a built-in renderer's document, to run nested (`embedRenderer`); rejects with the host's reason when it supplies none (see `RendererClient.requestDocument`). |
| `schedule` | `"schedule": Array<ScheduledStep>` | The comparison's steps on the progress axis for the direction this transition presents (see `DirectionLatch`). Empty for extractions. |
| `scope` | `"scope": ScopeView \| undefined` | The Changes scope, while the host shows a comparison's changes and their context (`changesScope`): its `shown` items, with the parts the person opened (`expand`). A list folds the rest (`useFolds`, `Fold`); a canvas that declares `MountOptions.scope` `subset` receives a `model` of only what is shown and lays that out. Nothing is faded: what is shown is drawn at full strength, and what isn't takes no room. Undefined while every item is shown. |
| `selectedId` | `"selectedId": null \| string` | The selected item's ID (an entity row ID, or a part's `data-entity-id`), or `null` when nothing is selected. |
| `setControl` | `"setControl": { (id: string, value: false \| number \| string \| true): void }` | Sets a declared control from the renderer's own content, as the person changed it there (a sortable column header): the host applies it as if they had set it in its settings, remembers it and sends it back in `controls`. The new value shows at once. |
| `viewport` | `"viewport": undefined \| { "height": number; "width": number }` | The frame's width and the host window's height, CSS px, as the host last reported them; undefined until then. |

### `StatusTab`

```ts
StatusTab(__0: { "change": { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }; "emphasis": number; "measure"?: false | true }): Element
```

A pill's or chip's status as a tab hanging off its bottom edge: the icon and
word per part, filled and edged in the status hue, joined to the pill and
rounded on its free corners. Render it inside the pill (positioned:
`position: relative` or otherwise), which keeps its single-line box; the
pill's container reserves `--pk-tab-height` below every pill, so nothing
moves when status appears, but an unchanged pill draws nothing there. The
tab joins the pill at its left, its left side on the pill's left border and
the pill's bottom-left corner squared; the pill's content is centred. Where
the pill is too narrow to keep its bottom-right corner radius clear of the
tab, the tab spans the pill's full width, its sides on the pill's borders,
and both the pill's bottom corners are squared, so pill and tab read as one
shape. The squared corners and the hidden bottom edge follow the pill's
`--emphasis`, so they fade with the tab; the pill's corners are expected to
be `--projections-radius`. A pill must
be at least as wide as its tab: `measure` draws the tab at full strength
and its natural width, for measuring the room a pill needs (the wider of its
content and `.pk-status-tab`). It fades with `emphasis` and is absent at 0.
The pill's accessible name carries the status, so the tab is hidden from
assistive technology.

### `SvgChangeStatus`

```ts
SvgChangeStatus(__0: { "anchor"?: "end" | "middle" | "start"; "change": { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }; "emphasis": number; "parts"?: Array<StatusPart> | undefined; "room"?: number | undefined; "x": number; "y": number }): Element | null
```

`StatusText` for SVG cards: one line at `x`, `y` (the text baseline) with
an icon and a word per part, for the card's own reserved footer band:
starting at `x`, ending there, or centred on it (`anchor`), never wider
than `room` (its last words end in an ellipsis instead, whole in its
tooltip). Words are measured in the font they are drawn in, so a centred
line is centred exactly from its first frame. Empty at zero emphasis.

### `SvgFooterRow`

```ts
SvgFooterRow(__0: { "children": Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise<Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | ReactElement<unknown, string | { (props: any): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise | Promise<ReactNode> | ReactElement<unknown, recursive> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined } | { new (props: any, context: any): Component<any, any, any> }> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined> | ReactElement<unknown, string | { (props: any): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise<Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | ReactElement<unknown, recursive> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined> | Promise<ReactNode> | ReactElement | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined } | { new (props: any, context: any): Component<any, any, any> }> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined; "className"?: string | undefined; "x"?: number; "y": number }): Element
```

One row of an SVG card's footer band, such as a change line (`Lifetime Scoped → Singleton`) above the status:
centred on `x` (by default 0, the middle of a card drawn about its centre) at the baseline `y`, as the status line
is (`SvgChangeStatus` with `anchor="middle"`), so every row of the band shares one axis. Its `children` are the
row's `tspan`s (spacing between them with `dx` is centred with them). Lay its text out within
`cardFooterRoom(width)`, wrapping longer text onto more rows, so it never reaches the card's sides.

### `SvgIcon`

```ts
SvgIcon(__0: { "className"?: string; "name": "added" | "additive" | "agent" | "application" | "blocked" | "breaking" | "bytecode" | "changed" | "collapse" | "comparator" | "compatible" | "credential" | "downgraded" | "enforced" | "error" | "exclude" | "expand" | "extractor" | "file" | "generated" | "hidden" | "host" | "import" | "include" | "info" | "modified" | "module" | "moved" | "namespace" | "network" | "other" | "policy" | "process" | "read" | "redeploy" | "removed" | "renamed" | "renderer" | "replace" | "rescoped" | "settings" | "unenforced" | "unknown" | "upgraded" | "varied" | "visible" | "warning" | "workload"; "size": number; "x": number; "y": number }): Element
```

An icon inside SVG: a `size` square whose top-left corner is at `x`, `y`,
drawn in the SVG's `color`. It is SVG throughout (a rect in `currentColor`
under an SVG mask of the icon's images, which the SDK's `icons.css`
resolves from the theme tokens), so it follows every transform the
drawing is under: CSS masks inside a `foreignObject` don't in WebKit. A
badge is its disc with the glyph cut out.

### `SvgValueChange`

```ts
SvgValueChange(__0: { "after": string; "anchor"?: "end" | "middle" | "start"; "before": string; "className"?: string; "x": number; "y": number } & Record<`data-${string}`, string>): Element
```

`ValueChange` inside SVG: one text line at `x`, `y` (the baseline) with
the old value struck through in the removed hue, an arrow, then the new
value in the added hue. Pass identifier attributes (the SDK's
`identifier`) for code values such as versions.

```ts
interface TablePropsSource
```

What `useTableProps` reads from a kit renderer's props.

| Member | Signature | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `comparing` | `"comparing": false \| true` | Whether this is a comparison (`RendererProps.comparing`). |
| `controls` | `"controls": { [key: string]: false \| number \| string \| true }` | The declared controls' values, the sort among them (`RendererProps.controls`). |
| `diff` | `"diff": false \| true` | Whether the host shows the comparison in diff mode (`RendererProps.diff`). |
| `emphasis` | `"emphasis": { (row: TableRow<unknown> & { "id"?: string }): number }` | A row's change emphasis (`RendererProps.emphasis`). |
| `locale` | `"locale": string` | BCP 47 locale for numbers and comparing strings (`RendererProps.locale`). |
| `onSelect` | `"onSelect": { (id: null \| string): void }` | Selects an item (`RendererProps.onSelect`). |
| `progress` | `"progress": number` | The frame's progress, 0 (Before) to 1 (After) (`RendererProps.progress`). |
| `scope` | `"scope"?: ChangesScope \| undefined` | The Changes scope, which the table folds by (`RendererProps.scope`). |
| `selectedId` | `"selectedId": null \| string` | The host's selection (`RendererProps.selectedId`). |
| `setControl` | `"setControl": { (id: string, value: false \| number \| string \| true): void }` | Sets a control from the content, as a heading does the sort (`RendererProps.setControl`). |

### `useBorderWidths`

```ts
useBorderWidths(ref: RefObject<Element | null>): BorderWidths
```

The border widths in effect on a rendered element, read when it mounts (before its first paint); the defaults until then.

### `useContentAspect`

```ts
useContentAspect(ratio: number | undefined): void
```

Reports the shape (width / height) of the content a renderer fits to its stage, over the whole transition, so a
host can arrange held panes (side by side or stacked) for the larger fitted scale. `useFitScale` reports it; call
this from a renderer that fits content another way. Nothing is reported while `ratio` is undefined.

### `useControlActions`

```ts
useControlActions(onAction: { (listener: { (id: string): void }): { (): void } }, handlers: { [key: string]: { (): void } }): void
```

Runs `handlers[id]` when the host activates the declared action control
`id`, for as long as the component is mounted.

### `useCoveredPadding`

```ts
useCoveredPadding<P extends FitPadding>(stage: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, size: undefined | { "height": number; "width": number }, padding: P, maxScale?: number): P
```

`padding` for content of `size` fitted to the stage element `stage` (as `useFitScale` fits it), with its top moved
down and its bottom (`y`) up only where the host's cover (`useStageCover`) would otherwise lie over the fitted
drawing (see `coveredTop` and `coveredBottom`): a flat graph centred below a pane's chips and above a floating
summary keeps its own padding, a tall one opens between them. Without a cover, `padding` as it is. Pass the result
to `useFitScale` and pad the drawing's top by its `top` and its bottom by its `y` (the kit's `--pk-fit-top` and
`--pk-fit-bottom`, which graph.css reads). The stage is measured in the frame on every resize.

### `useDomainIndex`

```ts
useDomainIndex(model: ComparisonModel<Extraction>, progress: number, options?: { "include"?: ReadonlySet<string> | undefined; "presence"?: undefined | { (row: EntityChange<Entity>, progress: number): number } }): DomainIndex
```

Domain renderers group entities by their relationships rather than by
position; they all need rows keyed by identity and relationships resolved to
those rows. `presence` defaults to linear fades; staged renderers pass their
timeline's presence instead.

### `useFitScale`

```ts
useFitScale(stage: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, size: undefined | { "height": number; "width": number }, options?: FitOptions): Fit
```

Fits content of `size` (in its own units) to the stage element `stage`,
the flexible child of a filling renderer (see `useFrameFill`): centred and
scaled down to fit both dimensions, however small that makes it (the user
can zoom in, see `useStageZoom`), never above `maxScale`. Reports the height
a content-sized host should give the frame: the stage at the width-fitted
scale (or at `options.floor` when that is larger and the view opens there)
plus everything around it, but never more than the host's `stage-max-height` (`useStageHeightCap`), when it sends
one: content taller than that is fitted to the capped stage instead (or opens at the text floor and pans). Zoomed in
(`options.drawnScale`), it asks for the content's height at that scale, up to the same cap. Measured before paint and on every resize;
a new measurement holds the host's paint acknowledgement until the content
is drawn at its scale, so a host never measures a scale about to change
(such as the one before the renderer fills its frame).

### `useFolds`

```ts
useFolds<T>(items: Array<T>, idOf: { (item: T): string }, scope: ChangesScope | undefined): { "collapse": { (key: string): void }; "entries": Array<{ "item": T; "type": "item" } | { "items": Array<T>; "key": string; "open"?: false | true; "type": "fold" }>; "expand": { (key: string): void } }
```

Folds a list for the Changes scope (`foldList`) and keeps which folds the person expanded, until the scope's shown
items change. Without a scope every item is listed.

### `useFrameFill`

```ts
useFrameFill(preferredHeight: number | undefined): void
```

While the calling component is mounted, the renderer fills its frame's
height (`.pk[data-fill]`, a flex column whose child takes the remaining
height) and reports `preferredHeight` (CSS px) as its content height: the
height a host that sizes its frame to the content should give it. A host
that sizes the frame itself ignores the report, and the content still fills
the frame. Nothing is reported while `preferredHeight` is undefined.

### `useFrameSizing`

```ts
useFrameSizing(): "content" | "fill" | undefined
```

How the host sizes the frame (`RendererEnvironment.sizing`): `content` when it gives the frame the height the
renderer reports, so content fitted to it need only fit its width; `fill` when it sizes the frame itself; undefined
when the host doesn't say.

### `useFrameViewport`

```ts
useFrameViewport(): undefined | { "height": number; "width": number }
```

The frame's width and the host window's height, CSS px, as the host last reported them (`viewport`); undefined
until it has. A content-sized frame lies in its host's scrolling page, so the window's height bounds how tall a
stage that pans and zooms should ask to be (see `useFitScale`).

### `useLegend`

```ts
useLegend(report: { (legend: RendererLegend): void }, legend: RendererLegend | undefined): void
```

Reports the renderer's legend to the host whenever its content changes; the
host draws it once beside every pane. Pass `undefined` (or no items) to
clear it; unmounting clears it too. Describe the whole document, not the current progress, so the
legend never changes while scrubbing.

### `useOpeningFloor`

```ts
useOpeningFloor(root: RefObject<Element | null>, key: unknown): number
```

The scale at which the smallest text in `root` is drawn at `openingFloorPx`, or 0 before there is any: SVG text
and HTML text (including HTML in a `foreignObject`), whatever its opacity (text that fades in while scrubbing
counts), in content units, so `root` is the content the stage scales, whether by an SVG's size or a CSS transform.
Visually hidden HTML text (laid out at most 1 px wide or high, like `.sr-only`) doesn't count. Measured before paint
whenever `key` changes, for example the content's layout, never while scrubbing.

### `usePaintGate`

```ts
usePaintGate(ready: false | true): void
```

Holds the shell's `rendered` acknowledgement while `ready` is false, for a
component that paints asynchronously (for example after a layout). The host
keeps the frame hidden until the first acknowledgement, so the person never
sees a half-drawn first frame, and waits for each one before the next seek.

### `usePaintHold`

```ts
usePaintHold(): { (): { (): void } }
```

The shell's hold on its `rendered` acknowledgement (see `usePaintGate`), for
a hold taken outside React's render, such as in a `ResizeObserver` whose
measurement re-renders only later: call it to hold, and the function it
returns to release. Outside a kit renderer it holds nothing.

### `useScrollAnchor`

```ts
useScrollAnchor(scroller: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, scale: number, opening?: false | true, start?: { "x": number; "y": number } | { (view: { "height": number; "scale": number; "width": number }): { "left": number; "top": number } }, onMove?: undefined | { (): void }, clearCover?: false | true): { (): void }
```

Keeps the point at the middle of a scroll container in the middle when the
content's scale changes (fit, zoom, resize). While `opening` (the person has
neither zoomed nor scrolled), content that overflows stays at `start` (by
default its top left, where reading begins) rather than cut through the middle.
`onMove` is called when the person first scrolls, drags, taps or presses a
scroll key in content that overflows: the moment they start to pan.
Returns a function that keeps the view where its caller just scrolled it.

### `useScrolledPadding`

```ts
useScrolledPadding<P extends FitPadding>(padding: P, drawnScale: number, fitScale: number, height?: undefined | { "content": number; "view": number }): P
```

The padding a fitted drawing is drawn with (its `--pk-fit-top` and `--pk-fit-bottom`): `padding` while it is drawn
at its fitted scale (`fitScale`), and once it is drawn larger and scrolls down (opened at the text floor, or zoomed
in: `drawnScale`), under a cover a top of at least the host's `stage-inset-top` and a bottom (`y`) of at least its
`stage-inset-bottom`, so its first row opens, and its last row scrolls, clear of what the host overlays at the
frame's top and foot. `height` is the content's height (content units) and the stage's inner height (`Fit.height`):
a drawing drawn larger that still fits the stage's height (a flat graph zoomed in) keeps its padding where, centred,
it clears the bands, and takes just enough more where it doesn't (`scrolledPadding`), so it moves no more than it
must as it zooms. The fit never reads it.

### `useStageCover`

```ts
useStageCover(): Array<CoverRect> | undefined
```

The rectangles of the frame the host overlays (its `stage-cover` theme token, see `parseStageCover`), CSS px from
the frame's top left, or undefined when it sends none. A fitted canvas keeps clear of them only where its drawing
would reach them (`useCoveredPadding`); content that scrolls pads by `stage-inset-top` instead.

### `useStageHeightCap`

```ts
useStageHeightCap(): number | undefined
```

The most, CSS px, a content-sized stage that pans and zooms asks its host for (see `contentHeightCap`), from the
host's optional `stage-max-height` theme token and its viewport; undefined when the host sends no such token. A host
that sends it lays the frame in its scrolling page: such a stage also pans by dragging, leaving the wheel to the page.

### `useStageInset`

```ts
useStageInset(): number | undefined
```

The host's `stage-inset` theme token in CSS px (the space between the frame's edges and the content on the stage,
on every side), or undefined when the host sends none and the renderer keeps its own. CSS reads it through the kit's
stage padding (`pk-stage`, `--pk-stage-padding`); this is for layout computed in script, such as a fitted canvas's
padding.

### `useStageInsetBottom`

```ts
useStageInsetBottom(): number | undefined
```

The host's `stage-inset-bottom` theme token in CSS px (the space between the content and the frame's bottom edge,
where the host overlays the frame's foot, for example with a floating legend and summary), or undefined when it
sends none. CSS reads it through the kit's stage padding (`--pk-stage-padding-bottom`).

### `useStageInsetTop`

```ts
useStageInsetTop(): number | undefined
```

The host's `stage-inset-top` theme token in CSS px (the space between the frame's top edge and the content, where
the host overlays the frame's top, for example with a pane's label chip), or undefined when the host sends none and
the renderer keeps its own top padding. CSS reads it through the kit's stage padding (`pk-stage`,
`--pk-stage-padding-top`, the larger of it and `stage-inset`); this is for layout computed in script, such as a
fitted canvas's padding.

### `useStageZoom`

```ts
useStageZoom(scroller: RefObject<HTMLElement | null>, onAction: { (listener: { (id: string): void }): { (): void } }, fit: number, options?: StageZoomOptions): StageZoom
```

Zoom for content fitted to the scroll container `scroller` at `fit` (see
`useFitScale`): the `zoomControls` actions, Ctrl/⌘-wheel and pinch in the
frame, and a scroll position that keeps its centre across scale changes.
The view opens fitted, with everything in view, unless that would draw its
smallest text below `openingFloorPx`: then it opens at `options.floor`,
scrolled to `options.start`, and the person pans the rest. Until the person
zooms or pans, a resize recomputes that opening from the new fit. Fit returns
to everything in view however small, and zooming out stops there, so
everything is always reachable. Once zoomed or panned, a resize keeps the
zoom multiple of the new fit.

### `useSummaryNouns`

```ts
useSummaryNouns(declare: { (nouns: undefined | { (kind: string, collection: "entities" | "relationships"): SummaryNoun | false | undefined } | { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun | false }): void }, nouns: undefined | { (kind: string, collection: "entities" | "relationships"): SummaryNoun | false | undefined } | { readonly [key: string]: SummaryNoun | false }): void
```

Names the renderer's kinds in the host's summary bar (`RendererProps.declareNouns`): `{package: {singular:
'workspace', plural: 'workspaces'}}`, `false` to leave a kind out. The kinds an object lists come first, in its
order. Pass a stable value (memoize a function); `undefined` returns to `MountOptions.nouns`.

### `useTableProps`

```ts
useTableProps(props: TablePropsSource, id?: string): { "changesFirst": false | true; "comparing": false | true; "diff": false | true; "emphasis": { (row: TableRow<unknown>): number }; "locale": string; "onSelect": { (id: string): void }; "onSortChange": { (next: { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" | "descending" }): void }; "progress": number; "scope": ChangesScope | undefined; "selectedId": null | string; "sort": null | { "column": string; "direction": "ascending" | "descending" } }
```

A `DataTable`'s props from a kit renderer's (`RendererProps`): the comparison, mode, progress, emphasis, selection,
locale and Changes scope, and the sort held in the controls `tableSortControls` declares under `id` (`sort` by default), which a
heading's activation sets through the host, so the host remembers it, shows it in its settings and lets agents read
and set it. Spread them: `<DataTable {...useTableProps(props)} label columns rows />`.

### `ValueChange`

```ts
ValueChange(__0: { "after"?: Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise<Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | ReactElement<unknown, string | { (props: any): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise | Promise<ReactNode> | ReactElement<unknown, recursive> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined } | { new (props: any, context: any): Component<any, any, any> }> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined> | ReactElement<unknown, string | { (props: any): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise<Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | ReactElement<unknown, recursive> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined> | Promise<ReactNode> | ReactElement | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined } | { new (props: any, context: any): Component<any, any, any> }> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined; "before"?: Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise<Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | ReactElement<unknown, string | { (props: any): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise | Promise<ReactNode> | ReactElement<unknown, recursive> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined } | { new (props: any, context: any): Component<any, any, any> }> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined> | ReactElement<unknown, string | { (props: any): Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | Promise<Iterable<ReactNode, any, any> | ReactElement<unknown, recursive> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined> | Promise<ReactNode> | ReactElement | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined } | { new (props: any, context: any): Component<any, any, any> }> | ReactPortal | bigint | false | null | number | string | true | undefined; "className"?: string; "layout"?: "inline" | "stacked" }): Element
```

A value that changed: the old one struck through in a removed pill, then
the new one in an added pill, stacked (the default) or on one line with an
arrow. Assistive technology reads "was …, now …". A missing side shows
only the other pill.

### `VariedMarker`

```ts
VariedMarker(__0: { "change"?: { "renamed"?: false | true | undefined; "status": "added" | "modified" | "removed" | "unchanged"; "varied"?: Array<Varied> | undefined }; "emphasis"?: number }): Element | null
```

The volatile marker: a `modified` change with a volatile value beyond its
tolerance (the SDK's `variedBeyond`) shows the `varied` icon beside its
status. It is neutral, in the text color rather than a change color,
and named for assistive technology ("Volatile field changed beyond
tolerance"). It fades with the status it accompanies. Draws nothing for any
other change, so an item that varied only within tolerance stays unchanged.

### `ViewOptions`

```ts
type ViewOptions = { steps?: "schedule" | "manual"; scope?: { layout: "fold"; } | { layout: "subset"; parts?: ScopedParts; context?: (all: ComparisonModel<Extraction>, changes: ReadonlySet<string>, renderer: string) => Iterable<string>; }; controls?: readonly RendererControl[]; nouns?: SummaryNouns; facts?: SummaryFacts; interactions?: false; }
```

What a view module may export as `options` beside its `View`, for the entry `rendererConfig({view})` generates: the
mount options other than the name, capabilities and accepted extractions, which `rendererConfig` declares.

```tsx
export const options: ViewOptions = {nouns: {service: {singular: 'service', plural: 'services'}}}
```
